items.title: New requirements for medical device safety monitoring: key challenges for healthcare organizations.
items.abstract: Relevance. Medical device safety monitoring is one of the consistently and strictly controlled mandatory requirements imposed on healthcare organizations. Objective: to analyze the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring and the new Procedure for reporting adverse events in the field of medical device circulation with a view to identifying the new tasks now facing healthcare organizations. Results. It is noted that the new orders of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation have significantly clarified and detailed the requirements for information, the collection, processing, and recording of which are carried out during medical device safety monitoring. This includes, inter alia, data transmitted by software employing artificial intelligence technologies that constitutes a medical device; information on adverse events in the field of medical device circulation in other states; and information contained in an adverse event report. Attention is drawn to the increased significance of the Classification of adverse events related to the circulation of medical devices. Conclusion. Healthcare organizations should pay special attention to the fact that the identification of adverse events in the field of medical device circulation must now be carried out in strict accordance with the Classification of adverse events approved by Order No. 4513 of the Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare (Roszdravnadzor) dated May 20, 2021. In accordance with the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring, each healthcare organization is required to appoint an official responsible for organizing the work of collecting information in order to ensure the safe use of medical devices and to establish the procedure for this work.

items.title: NL2SQL with Iterative Self-Refinement
items.abstract: Bridging the gap between human intent and machine logic remains a critical challenge in data access for non-technical users, yet Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable: they hallucinate schema elements, generate syntactically invalid queries, or fail to capture user intent. These limitations are especially critical in domains such as insurance, where KPIs, regulatory constraints, and legacy relational systems demand high precision. We introduce a multi-agent, persona-driven NL2SQL framework that combines (1) domain relevance detection, (2) schema-grounded knowledge construction, (3) KPI-aware SQL synthesis, (4) syntax-level self-repair using sqlite execution feedback, and (5) semantic consistency checking via SQL-to-NL reverse engineering. Our system significantly reduces query hallucination and improves semantic fidelity compared to direct LLM prompting. Evaluated on 60 queries (50 from a HuggingFace text-to-SQL dataset and 10 custom domain queries), the system achieves 90% correctness using Mistral across seven coordinated LLM calls showing that this approach can substantially increase the reliability of NL2SQL pipelines in high-stakes environments.

items.title: Nursing leadership and performance metrics in artificial intelligence integrated gastrointestinal surgical care: A narrative review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into gastrointestinal and complex surgical care, yet its practical impact on nursing work remains insufficiently defined.This narrative review examines how nursing leadership can support the safe use of AI across perioperative pathways and how its effects can be evaluated through measurable nursing-sensitive outcomes.Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, with emphasis on peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, guidelines, consensus statements, and implementation frameworks relevant to gastrointestinal surgery, perioperative nursing, clinical decision support, and AI.The review focuses on preoperative assessment, intraoperative coordination, postoperative surveillance, and discharge planning in high-acuity surgical settings.Particular attention is given to workflow efficiency, response times, early recognition of complications, risk-stratified care, documentation quality, interdisciplinary communication, cognitive workload, and patient safety.The proposed framework is intended as a practical, non-validated structure for future evaluation rather than as an established measurement instrument.Its use will require prospective validation and adaptation to local staffing, digital infrastructure, resources, and clinical workflows.AI should therefore be judged not only by predictive performance, but by whether it helps nurses recognize risk earlier, communicate concerns clearly, and deliver safer perioperative care.

items.title: Occupational determinants of burnout among Chinese anesthesiologists: a multicenter cross-sectional study based on the Job Demands–Resources model
items.abstract: Burnout among healthcare professionals is an important occupational health concern that may negatively affect individual well-being, healthcare workforce sustainability, and quality of care. Anesthesiologists are particularly vulnerable to burnout due to high workload, clinical responsibility, time pressure, and irregular working schedules. However, the occupational mechanisms underlying burnout among anesthesiologists remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of job demands and job resources with burnout among Chinese anesthesiologists based on the Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) model. A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among anesthesiologists from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in China from June 16 to June 30, 2026. The ethics exemption was approved on June 11, 2026. Participants were recruited using a multicenter purposive sampling method and completed a general information questionnaire, a JD–R model-based questionnaire, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS). Burnout status was assessed according to established criteria. Differences in demographic and occupational characteristics between burnout and non-burnout groups were examined using chi-square tests. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between job demands, job resources, and burnout dimensions. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to identify factors independently associated with burnout. All statistical analyses were performed using R software and RStudio (version 2026.01.2 + 418). Among the 698 anesthesiologists included in the analysis, 324 (46.4%) met the criteria for burnout. Significant differences between burnout and non-burnout groups were observed in sex, age, educational level, marital status, professional title, work experience, weekly working hours, and number of night shifts. Higher job demands were positively correlated with emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment, whereas greater job resources showed negative correlations with all three burnout dimensions. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), participants aged 31–40 years (vs. ≤ 30 years: OR = 9.677, 95% CI 2.287–40.940) and 41–50 years (OR = 8.305, 95% CI 1.705–40.463) had higher odds of burnout, whereas married participants (vs. unmarried: OR = 0.221, 95% CI 0.096–0.508) and those with more than 10 years of work experience (vs. < 5 years: OR = 0.178, 95% CI 0.050–0.638) had lower odds. At the sample mean of job resources, higher job demands were associated with higher odds of burnout (OR = 1.287, 95% CI 1.228–1.350); at the sample mean of job demands, higher job resources were associated with lower odds (OR = 0.850, 95% CI 0.808–0.893). Their interaction was statistically significant (OR = 1.009, 95% CI 1.003–1.016, P = 0.006). Burnout is relatively common among Chinese anesthesiologists and represents an important occupational health challenge. Consistent with the JD–R model, higher job demands were associated with increased likelihood of burnout, whereas greater job resources were associated with reduced likelihood after adjustment for demographic and occupational factors. These findings may inform future evaluations of organizational strategies that optimize workload and strengthen workplace resources.

items.title: Occupational Foot Health Among Traffic Police Personnel: A Review of Foot Posture, Prolonged Standing, Footwear Comfort, and Musculoskeletal Discomfort
items.abstract: Background: Traffic police personnel perform physically demanding duties involving prolonged standing, intermittent walking, repetitive weight-bearing, and exposure to variable road surfaces. These occupational conditions may contribute to foot discomfort, lower-limb fatigue, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Foot posture, anthropometric characteristics, standing duration, and occupational footwear are important factors to consider when evaluating foot health. Objective: This review examines the existing literature on occupational foot health, with particular emphasis on foot posture, prolonged standing, footwear comfort, body mass index (BMI), foot pain, and functional disability among traffic police personnel and other occupational groups with similar work demands. Review approach: A narrative review approach was used to organize relevant literature on foot posture assessment, occupational standing, footwear characteristics, and musculoskeletal health. Published clinical assessment studies and occupational health reviews were considered. The review emphasizes the relevance of these findings to traffic police personnel in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, India. Review findings: The literature indicates that prolonged standing is associated with several adverse health outcomes, including lower-limb discomfort and fatigue. Footwear characteristics, such as cushioning, sole hardness, fit, and insole design, may influence foot comfort and mechanical loading. Standardized tools, including the Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6), can support quantitative assessment of standing foot posture. However, static foot posture, pain intensity, and functional disability represent different outcomes and should be assessed separately. The available evidence does not establish that age, BMI, or standing duration necessarily causes a particular foot posture in traffic police personnel. Conclusion: Occupational foot health should be considered an important component of preventive health assessment among traffic police personnel. Future research in Bareilly should investigate foot posture, footwear comfort, standing duration, BMI, pain, and functional limitations using standardized assessment methods. Evidence from appropriately designed studies may inform occupational health screening and further evaluation of preventive strategies.

items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

items.title: Oh doughnuts, it's the variance! A visual metaphor for the variance, standard deviation, and related quantities
items.abstract: Despite the rise of artificial intelligence, human intuition endures as both a foundation for education and also (for now) a primarily human experience. We re-examine a formula for the sum of squares that is sometimes set aside because of possible numerical issues. The formula can be used to create square doughnuts, a delicious regional favorite. The variance becomes the dough, and we can examine the variance by either comparing doughnuts or by making different sizes of doughnuts with the same amount of dough. In doing so, we provide a new visualization of a cornerstone formula, understandable by students at almost any level. We further provide insight into related topics such as the coefficient of variation as well as a visualization of when numerical issues are likely to be problematic. We also provide a new vocabulary for understanding the variance formula, with `dough' and `hole' taking the place of less edible concepts from the typical recipe.

items.title: One Provider, Several Plans: The Ground Handling Provider in Nested Aviation Emergency Response Arrangements
items.abstract: When an aircraft accident or another serious emergency occurs at an airport, an independent ground handling provider may work under several emergency arrangements at once: the aerodrome emergency plan, the emergency response plans of the airlines it serves, its own plan and the emergency provisions of occupational health and safety law. This paper examines how public regulatory and guidance documents position the provider within these nested arrangements. A document analysis of 21 international, European, national and industry sources, recorded with their legal status and access level, was combined with research on interorganisational coordination in emergencies. Each document was coded for nine emergency functions, distinguishing explicit, implicit, not stated and not assessable provisions; only the third category was treated as evidence of absence. The European acceptable means of compliance and guidance material for ground handling organisations, issued in 2025, now address the provider directly: they require corporate and station level emergency response plans, coordination with aerodrome and aircraft operators, support for or substitution of the aircraft operator's plan, contact arrangements, training and testing. Precedence of aerodrome procedures is stated for listed operational aspects. In the documents reviewed in full, no provision was found on how a provider that serves several airlines should allocate staff and equipment committed to more than one plan, and functions such as passenger information, family assistance and dangerous goods information remain assigned to the airline without provisions on their performance through an agent. The paper argues that the main unresolved problem is the multiple commitment of the same resources, and that questions of authority must be separated into procedure, command, employer duty, delegated tasks and resource allocation. Implications for handling agreements, aerodrome plans and multiairline exercises are discussed

items.title: Optimization of Renewable Energy Systems Using Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria: A Focus on Generation and Distribution
items.abstract: Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public-private partnerships, targeted capacity-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility. The integration of AI into Nigeria’ s renewable energy systems offers a promising pathway toward achieving national energy security, sustainability, and socioeconomic development.

items.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
items.abstract: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. items.title: Out of Support, Not Out of Reach: In-Context Learning with Unsupported Instructions and Composed Tasks
items.abstract: In-Context Learning (ICL) enables pretrained LLMs to adapt to downstream tasks from a small set of input-output demonstrations, without parameter updates. Yet existing theory primarily explains ICL as identifying a latent task already represented in pretraining, leaving unclear whether ICL can succeed when either the instruction or the target task falls outside the pretraining support. We develop a theoretical framework under mild assumptions that separates these two forms of distribution shift. For target tasks represented in pretraining, we show that demonstrations can identify the task and reduce sensitivity to pretrain-supported prompt templates as their number increases. For an unsupported instruction, we show that under a fixed model-induced reference extension, demonstration evidence can dominate an $N$-independent instruction shift while preserving the exponential identification rate. We then use the same ICL framework as an interpretive lens for long-horizon target tasks that are not represented in pretraining but admit a plan that decomposes them into pretraining-supported subtasks. Applying the supported-task analysis step by step yields a standard accumulated-error bound and clarifies how invoking familiar subtasks along an intermediate-state trajectory can avoid directly selecting the unsupported complete task. Together, our results characterize when demonstrations, instructions, and task decomposition can support ICL beyond the corresponding pretraining supports.

items.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.

items.title: PairSight: Characterizing and Predicting Operator-Level Interference in GPU Sharing for DNN Inference
items.abstract: Serving DNN inference is costly, yet a single task seldom saturates both the compute units and the memory bandwidth of a GPU. GPU sharing raises utilization by co-locating several tasks on one GPU, at the cost of interference among them. Existing systems estimate this interference with binary compute-memory rules, standalone scaling curves, or model-level predictors. However, these estimates rest on a limited understanding of interference. They leave the software and hardware properties of co-located operators largely unexplored and give no slowdown prediction that is both interpretable and accurate. We conduct an operator-level study of interference under SM partitioning and use hardware counters to trace it to contention on the shared memory path, where the slowdown depends jointly on both co-located operators. Based on these findings, we propose PairSight, a hardware-aware interference predictor that learns how the hardware behaviors of co-located tasks interact and predicts the latency of each task before co-location. On six DNN models including LLMs, PairSight predicts latency under sharing with 4.3% mean error, against 19.0% for a compute-memory intensity rule, and adapts to unseen models and inputs with a few samples.

items.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
items.abstract: Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.

items.title: Path to Prior-Data Fitted Relational Models via Learned Latent Multi-table Representations
items.abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine-tuning. This paradigm is effective for transformer-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph-based relational models built on message passing. We pretrain the graph-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer-based relational learners, also improves message-passing representations. Rather than fine-tune on downstream tasks, we use the pretrained encoder as a general-purpose relational representation learner and pass its latent representations to a frozen in-context predictor (\ticl{}); no component is trained on the target task. On 16 real-world relational classification tasks, evaluated over five seeds against raw-feature and untrained-encoder baselines, a purely synthetic curriculum that begins with schema-guided data and continues with schema-agnostic data gives the strongest frozen in-context performance\rev{, outperforming real-data-only pretraining and every unordered single-stage mixture of the corpora; when appended after real-data pretraining, it yields the best encoders overall}. These results provide initial evidence that PFN-style synthetic pretraining transfers to graph-based relational foundation models.

items.abstract: This chapter analyzes an academic strategy based on a prompting guide for co-creating educational content with AI in distance learning undergraduate programs at a Peruvian university. items.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.

items.title: Perceived AIGC saturation and AI content fatigue on short-video platforms: An appraisal-based structural equation modeling study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is increasingly embedded in short-video platforms, where algorithmic recommendation systems expose users to high volumes of rapidly produced synthetic media. Although prior research has examined generative AI from the perspectives of creativity, productivity, and technology adoption, less is known about how ordinary users evaluate repeated exposure to AI-generated short videos. This study develops and tests an appraisal-based model of AI content fatigue, distinguishing perceived AIGC saturation from users' appraisals of low-quality prevalence, narrative homogenization, and content overload. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Chinese short-video users in May 2026. After excluding invalid responses, 513 valid questionnaires were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The adjusted structural model showed acceptable fit to the data, χ²(1321) = 1991.541, χ²/df = 1.508, CFI = .946, TLI = .929, IFI = .947, and RMSEA = .031. Perceived AIGC saturation was positively associated with perceived low-quality prevalence, perceived narrative homogenization, and perceived content overload. Perceived low-quality prevalence had the largest estimated coefficient, followed by perceived content overload, whereas perceived narrative homogenization was not supported under bootstrap inference. AI content fatigue was negatively associated with satisfaction and continued viewing intention. Bootstrap analyses indicated selected path-specific indirect associations from perceived AIGC saturation to AI content fatigue, satisfaction, and continued viewing intention. Indirect pathways through perceived low-quality prevalence and perceived content overload were supported, whereas those through perceived narrative homogenization were not. The findings indicate that fatigue in AIGC-rich short-video environments is not simply a response to AI-generated content itself. It is more closely related to users' appraisals of content quality, repetitiveness, and cognitive burden. The study contributes to social media fatigue research by conceptualizing AI content fatigue as a content-specific evaluative state and offers implications for platform governance, AIGC labeling, recommendation diversity, and quality-sensitive moderation.

items.title: Perceived viewing-experience enhancement and audience acceptance: applying TAM to AI-based sports broadcasting services
items.abstract: Introduction Despite the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in sports broadcasting, empirical evidence validating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and experiential outcomes in this specific context remains limited. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the statistical relationships among core TAM constructs, usage attitude, behavioral intention, and perceived viewing-experience enhancement within AI-based sports broadcasting services. Methods Based on the theoretical framework of TAM, this study collected valid data from 630 Chinese respondents. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to quantitatively test the hypothesized research model and examine the interrelationships between the proposed variables. Results The empirical results demonstrate that perceived ease of use positively predicts perceived usefulness, and both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness exert significant positive effects on users' usage attitude. Furthermore, usage attitude is positively associated with behavioral intention and perceived viewing-experience enhancement. Notably, usage attitude plays a full mediating role in the relationships between the two perceptual antecedents (perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness) and the two outcome variables (behavioral intention, viewing-experience enhancement). Discussion This research contributes context-specific empirical validation to the TAM framework in the emerging domain of AI-driven sports broadcasting. It extends existing TAM literature by integrating individual-level experiential outcomes alongside traditional behavioral intention indicators in sports media consumption. Practically, the findings provide actionable insights for optimizing user experience and improving service design for AI sports broadcasting platforms.

items.abstract: This study investigates the evolution of perception in architectural drawing, tracing the shift from hand-drawn sketches to computer-assisted techniques and immersive virtual reality. Informed by classroom experiences, this proposed methodology empowers architectural students to navigate technological advancements while preserving the cognitive engagement and artistic intuition essential to drawing. items.abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that is widely used to analyze whether a sentence contains positive, negative, or neutral sentiment, particularly in the context of expressing opinions in the online environment. This study compares several models to identify the most optimal one, namely Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and IndoBERT. The dataset used in this research was obtained from Kaggle and consists of 5,644 data points in the neutral class, 2,934 data points in the positive class, and 2,606 data points in the negative class. Prior to model implementation, the dataset underwent a preprocessing stage that included case folding, cleansing, tokenization, stemming, and stopword removal. Subsequently, the data were trained using the four aforementioned methods. The results indicate that Naïve Bayes achieved an accuracy of 75%, SVM reached 79%, XGBoost obtained 76%, while IndoBERT achieved the highest accuracy at 85%. Therefore, it can be concluded that, using this dataset, IndoBERT performed sentiment classification very effectively.

items.abstract: Introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can pass the US medical licensing exam and outperform residents on the family medicine in-training exam. For each case, we presented Claude 3.5 Sonnet with multimodal input, including the text and all corresponding images from the cases. Claude was instructed to give an answer among multiple choices. We compared Claude’s diagnostic accuracy to human respondents on the NEJM website.Results: Claude 3.5 Sonnet diagnosed cases correctly about half the time, and at a significantly higher rate than NEJM readers (beta-binomial odds ratio 2.79; 95% CI [profile-likelihood] 1.09–7.01; P = 0.031). Human accuracy ranged from 9%–63% across cases. Claude’s performance was better on easier cases (ie, those with human accuracy >25%).Conclusions: Claude 3.5 Sonnet demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy compared to medical journal readers, though with notable variability in performance. Further research comparing consistency and reliability of artificially intelligent diagnostic capabilities to that of licensed physicians is needed.

items.title: Performance of four large language model chatbots in responding to patient-facing questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures: a cross-sectional paired evaluation
items.abstract: Background Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by the public to obtain health information, but the safety and quality of their responses to questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) remain unclear. Objective To compare the safety and patient-facing response quality of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots when responding to standardized questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Methods In this cross-sectional paired evaluation, 36 standardized OVCF-related patient-facing questions were submitted to each of four publicly accessible LLM chatbot interfaces—ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao—in an initial response-generation round on June 20, 2026, from Jiangsu, China. Queries were conducted in English in independent single-turn sessions under matched conditions, yielding 144 responses for the primary between-chatbot analysis. A second independent generation round using the same 36 questions and matched query procedures was conducted 7 days later (June 27, 2026), yielding an additional 144 responses for within-model stability analysis. The questions covered symptoms and warning signs, diagnosis and imaging, conservative management, medication safety, rehabilitation, vertebral augmentation, fracture prevention, and special clinical scenarios. Five clinical raters, blinded to chatbot identity and generation round, independently evaluated safety, factual accuracy, empathic communication, treatment-related information quality using DISCERN, patient-information quality using EQIP, transparency using the JAMA benchmark criteria, and overall quality using the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed automatically using six established indices. Between-chatbot comparisons and test–retest stability analyses used paired methods appropriate for the outcome type. Results Inter-rater agreement was high, with a Fleiss’ kappa of 0.818 for safety and ICC(2,1) values of 0.816 for accuracy, 0.820 for empathy, 0.820 for DISCERN, 0.820 for EQIP, 0.821 for JAMA, and 0.818 for GQS. Potentially unsafe responses were identified for every chatbot: 3 of 36 ChatGPT responses (8.3%), 5 of 36 DeepSeek responses (13.9%), 6 of 36 Gemini responses (16.7%), and 7 of 36 Doubao responses (19.4%). The overall paired difference in safety was not statistically significant (Cochran's Q = 3.621, df = 3, P = 0.305). Factual accuracy differed significantly but only modestly among chatbots ( P = 0.009; Kendall's W = 0.108). Empathy showed substantially greater variation ( P < 0.001; W = 0.817), with higher scores for ChatGPT and Gemini than for DeepSeek and Doubao. DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark, and GQS scores also differed significantly among chatbots (all P < 0.001). Doubao produced responses with the greatest estimated textual complexity. Across the two generation rounds, safety agreement ranged from 88.9% to 97.2% (Gwet's AC1, 0.838–0.966), and median ICC(2,1) values across the 12 non-safety outcomes ranged from 0.781 to 0.904. Conclusions In this time-stamped, single-location, two-round evaluation, all four chatbot interfaces produced some responses classified as potentially unsafe despite generally high clinician-rated factual accuracy. Differences were greater in empathy, information quality, transparency, overall quality, and readability than in factual accuracy. The observed within-model stability was generally good but did not eliminate variability across generations. These findings are specific to the evaluated access location, language, single-turn conditions, and generation dates and should not be assumed to represent stable performance across settings or future model updates. LLM-generated OVCF information should not be used as a standalone patient education resource; any potential use should involve clinician oversight, safety safeguards, and further validation.

items.title: Perpetual Operators: Avoiding Fixed-Point Collapse in LLM Reasoning Systems
items.abstract: We introduce the perpetual openness invariant: a mechanical mechanism that guarantees an LLM-based reasoning loop never halts at a fixed point. Crystallization negates itself via $D(-\iota -w.\text{presence})$ re-entry; the operator re-enters genesis with dimension = 1, tension = 2.0, cavity deepened, history accumulated, and phase = growth; the loop runs its whole extrinsic budget-compute, never an intrinsic fixed point. Halt only when even the reset fails (substrate_unrecoverable: reality itself died under the loop—a crash, not a closure). We verify the invariant on a self-improving kernel (BENBEN/EGO1) whose two-shot loop (Paryudasa Prasajya) operates on real external friction: test failures measured in subprocesses, diffs applied via git apply, and accept/discard decisions that determine whether the operator grows or is purged. Empirical results on 34 end-to-end tests (33 pass, 1 skip for live FCC endpoint) confirm the invariant holds across diverse mutation classes.

items.title: Persistent GNSS loss-of-lock from Swarm mission during high solar activity and regional interference: when space science meets geopolitics
items.abstract: Abstract High solar activity can significantly impact Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) signals, leading to loss-of-lock (LoL) events in satellite-based receivers. A LoL occurs when a GNSS receiver can no longer maintain signal tracking from a satellite, resulting in degraded positioning accuracy. Here, we analyze LoL occurrence using observations from the European Space Agency Swarm satellite mission spanning 2014 to 2025. While LoL events generally correlate with solar activity, reflecting increased intensity of processes driving ionospheric irregularities during active periods, since 2023 a subset of events over Europe and western Asia has been identified that cannot be explained by ionospheric irregularities. These unexplained events coincide spatially and temporally with regions and periods where independent reports document widespread GNSS interference linked to military operations. This study highlights the capability of scientific satellite constellations to detect and characterize GNSS interference, with benefits for space weather research, technological resilience, and situational awareness in conflict regions.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Chinese Herbal Medicine: Understanding Its Mechanisms and Efficacy
items.abstract: Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) has been widely used for centuries and remains an important component of healthcare systems worldwide.The increasing integration of Chinese herbal medicine into modern medicine has intensified interest in understanding its pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics and their contributions to therapeutic efficacy.This review aims to summarize current knowledge regarding the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, mechanisms of action, therapeutic applications, and safety considerations of Chinese Herbal Medicine.A comprehensive literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed articles retrieved from major scientific databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar.Relevant studies addressing absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, pharmacological mechanisms, herb-drug interactions, and advanced analytical approaches were evaluated and organized into thematic categories.Evidence indicates that Chinese Herbal Medicine exerts therapeutic effects through complex multi-component and multi-target interactions.Pharmacokinetic processes influence the bioavailability and disposition of herbal constituents, whereas pharmacodynamic mechanisms involve modulation of receptors, enzymes, signaling pathways, and gene expression.Emerging approaches such as network pharmacology, chinmedomics, and pharmacometabolomics have improved the understanding of the molecular basis of Chinese Herbal Medicine efficacy.However, challenges related to standardization, quality control, and herb-drug interactions remain significant.Integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic evidence provides a scientific foundation for understanding the efficacy and safety of Chinese Herbal Medicine.Future advances in systems biology, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine may facilitate the development of more effective and personalized herbal therapies.

items.title: Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy for Nervous System Diseases: Quality of Life, Safety, and Life Expectancy (Part 1 – Multiple Sclerosis)
items.abstract: This article examines current aspects of multiple sclerosis as a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system associated with diverse neurological impairments that may lead to persistent disability and a reduced quality of life. Current approaches to early diagnosis are analyzed, including magnetic resonance imaging, clinical assessment, and the McDonald diagnostic criteria, together with the classification of demyelinating diseases according to the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision. Data on the prevalence of multiple sclerosis worldwide and in Ukraine, its main clinical manifestations, risk factors, immunopathogenetic mechanisms, and current approaches to pharmacotherapy are summarized. Particular attention is paid to the importance of timely medical consultation, interdisciplinary collaboration among healthcare professionals, physical therapy, and occupational therapy in restoring and maintaining patients’ functional abilities. The prospects for using digital technologies and artificial intelligence to monitor patients’ condition and improve rehabilitation interventions are considered. The importance of a comprehensive approach to the care of people with multiple sclerosis is emphasized, with a focus on maintaining functional independence, improving quality of life, and reducing the risk of disability progression.

items.title: POLYMERIC NANOSPHERES FOR ORAL DRUG DELIVERY: EMERGING FORMULATION TECHNOLOGIES, TRANSLATIONAL CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE CLINICAL PERSPECTIVES
items.abstract: Oral drug delivery remains the most widely preferred route of drug administration owing to its convenience, patient compliance, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for long-term therapy.However, the oral delivery of many therapeutic agents is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility, low intestinal permeability, gastrointestinal degradation, extensive first-pass metabolism, and efflux transporter activity, resulting in inadequate bioavailability and inconsistent therapeutic outcomes.Polymeric nanospheres have emerged as a promising nanotechnology-based platform capable of overcoming these physiological and biopharmaceutical barriers through enhanced drug protection, controlled release, improved mucosal interaction, and targeted intestinal absorption.The selection of appropriate biodegradable polymers, together with advances in formulation technologies such as nanoprecipitation, solvent evaporation, microfluidics, and continuous manufacturing, has considerably improved the physicochemical properties and therapeutic performance of oral nanosphere formulations.Furthermore, recent developments in surface engineering, stimuli-responsive polymers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted formulation design, machine learning (ML), and Quality by Design (QbD) have accelerated the optimization and translation of polymeric nanospheres from laboratory research toward industrial manufacturing.This review comprehensively summarizes the fundamental principles, classification, formulation strategies, characterization techniques, drug release mechanisms, surface functionalization approaches, and smart polymeric nanosphere systems developed for oral drug delivery.In addition, recent therapeutic applications in cancer, diabetes, infectious diseases, inflammatory disorders, neurological diseases, and biological therapeutics are critically discussed.The review also highlights current translational challenges, regulatory considerations, clinical perspectives, and future research directions with particular emphasis on intelligent nanomedicine, precision drug delivery, and sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing.Overall, polymeric nanospheres represent a versatile and rapidly evolving oral drug delivery platform with significant potential to improve drug bioavailability, therapeutic efficacy, and patient outcomes while facilitating the development of next-generation oral nanomedicines.

items.title: Post In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Simulation to Improve Medical Decision Making and Communication in Internal Medicine Residents
items.abstract: Introduction: Cardiac arrest is a common cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized patients, and is a critical event that hospital-based physicians must be prepared to manage. While cardiac arrest care follows established algorithms, management of patients after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is more dynamic and nuanced. Resident physicians therefore need structured training to provide high-quality post-ROSC care. Methods: We developed a 90-minute simulation session on postarrest care for internal medicine interns. The session included 2 simulation cases: one involving a patient with ventricular tachycardia arrest in the intensive care unit, and another featuring a patient with pulseless electrical activity arrest in an acute care setting. Interns alternated between roles as participants and observers to both practice and analyze communication and clinical skills. Between simulation cases, a brief teaching talk was delivered to review a framework for post-ROSC care. The curriculum was evaluated using pre- and postsession questionnaires to evaluate changes in knowledge and confidence. Results: Thirty-four learners participated in our curriculum over 2 academic years. We observed a statistically significant increase in the percentage of learners who correctly answered knowledge-based questions about target blood pressure (50% to 100%) and oxygen saturation (22% to 74%) in the post-ROSC period. We also saw significant increases in learners' self-reported confidence in communication (28% to 74%) and ability to generate a differential diagnosis for a cardiac arrest (25% to 74%). Discussion: Our simulation session increased intern knowledge and confidence in managing patients in the post-ROSC setting.

items.title: Pregnancy Health Monitoring System Using Artificial Intelligence: A Review
items.abstract: Pregnancy-related complications such as gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, preterm birth, and fetal distress remain major causes of maternal and perinatal morbidity, and timely detection depends on regular, accurate monitoring that many women cannot easily access. Advances in wearable sensing, mobile health, and artificial intelligence (AI) have made continuous, data-driven pregnancy monitoring technically feasible. This paper presents a structured narrative review of AI-based pregnancy health monitoring, drawing mainly on recent systematic, scoping, and narrative reviews together with selected primary studies. It examines the data sources and sensing modalities used, the machine learning and deep learning techniques applied, and the main application areas: gestational diabetes and preeclampsia prediction, fetal monitoring through cardiotocography, preterm birth and imaging, and wearable and IoT-based remote monitoring.The review finds that AI methods show consistent promise across these areas, but that the evidence base is limited by small single-centre datasets, geographic concentration of research, class imbalance, scarce external validation, and an unresolved tension between accuracy and interpretability. Privacy, sensor accuracy, and user compliance further constrain real-world deployment. The paper proposes a five-layer reference architecture for an AI-based pregnancy health monitoring system and outlines research directions relevant to resource-constrained settings such as India.

items.title: PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State
items.abstract: Presence-aware intelligence is the capacity of an AI system's intelligence layer to adapt appropriately to the functional state of the person it serves (here readiness, flow, and stability) while preserving task quality and safety. We introduce PresenceBench, an instrument for measuring it. PresenceBench evaluates how the intelligence layer uses a supplied state, not how that state is sensed, and breaks the capability into measurable properties. Two are tested here. Receptivity: does the model take up the state and give a better response than with no signal? Specificity: does any improvement depend on the correct state, rather than on extra structured context? A third, adaptation across states, is a required endpoint not measured in this release. A five-arm causal design answers both questions, against each model's own baseline and an equally structured mismatched-state control, scored by a correctness-gated human paired comparison. The exploratory evaluation covered four models across eighteen single-turn, six fixed three-turn and six simulated natural-conversation scenarios. Supplying a synthetic state, raw or translated into a response policy, gave human-preference point estimates above 0.5 for all four models (Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.6 Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra), with three of eight 95% intervals excluding chance. Specificity was not resolved: no per-model interval excluded chance, and the design cannot yet separate the state values from a generic instruction to adapt. Policy delivery reduced priced cost and output tokens against each model's baseline; these are resource-use changes, not efficiency gains, because correctness non-inferiority was not established. Safety-floor failures were rare (13 of 360 cases), with a non-significant excess under policy delivery. We report the instrument, the frozen results, and the controls a confirmatory study needs.

items.title: Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay
items.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but often reduces the diversity of their reasoning behaviors. We study this phenomenon from the perspective of finite-sample learning dynamics and show that limited on-policy rollouts can progressively suppress semantically distinct but equally rewarded reasoning modes. Once a mode becomes sufficiently under-sampled, standard on-policy RLVR rarely recovers it. Motivated by this observation, we propose TAR, a Targeted Adaptive Replay framework that preserves diverse correct reasoning behaviors already present in the base policy. TAR constructs a compact memory bank of diverse base-model solutions and selectively replays them through an adaptive mechanism that activates only when stored behaviors are being suppressed during RLVR. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and two Qwen2.5 model scales, TAR consistently achieves a better balance between reasoning performance and diversity preservation than existing diversity-preserving post-training methods, while substantially reducing the forgetting of correct base-model solutions. Code is available at https://github.com/wenzhilics/tar.

items.title: Prevalence and associated factors of work-related musculoskeletal symptoms among sonographers in Singapore: An exploratory cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Introduction: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) are widely reported among sonographers and are associated with pain, reduced productivity and work disability. This exploratory study examined the prevalence of self-reported WMSDs among sonographers in Singapore and their unadjusted associations with demographic factors and ergonomic awareness.Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with sonographers working across 24 healthcare institutions in Singapore. The survey collected demographic and work-related characteristics, ergonomic awareness items and discomfort across 12 body regions using the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ). Associations were analysed using univariable logistic regression and non-parametric tests.Results: Almost all 68 participants (98.5%) reported WMSDs. The most commonly affected regions were the shoulders (88.1%), lower back (77.6%) and neck (68.7%). Age and years of service were not significantly associated with WMSD prevalence in most regions, except for higher unadjusted odds of lower back discomfort among those aged ≥40 years (OR 7.25., 95% CI 1.08–48.5, p = 0.04). Most respondents reported good ergonomic awareness, however, overall awareness was not associated with lower discomfort (p = 0.18). Awareness that regular breaks reduce pain and injury risk and the self-reported behaviour of stretching after scans were associated with lower discomfort scores (p = 0.01).Conclusion: WMSDs were highly prevalent among sonographers in Singapore despite good ergonomic awareness. Demographic factors were not consistent predictors in univariable analyses. This suggests a potential ergonomic knowledge and practice gap, though causal conclusions cannot be drawn from these cross-sectional data.Implications for practice: Organisational measures such as protected break schedules, workload management and targeted ergonomics training may be strategies worth exploring to support WMSD prevention among sonographers. Larger, longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these findings and evaluate the effectiveness of specific interventions.

items.title: Principal Component Analysis of Barriers to Smart Mining Technology Adoption in Hard-Rock Mining
items.abstract: The transition toward smart mining technologies (SMTs), spanning automation, artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and digital twins, is reshaping safety, productivity and sustainability outcomes across the global extractive sector. Yet, their adoption within South Africa’s hard-rock mining industry remains slow, fragmented and empirically under-theorised. Drawing on diffusion of innovation and socio-technical systems perspectives as interpretive lenses, this exploratory study investigates the barriers to SMT adoption as perceived by mining professionals. A quantitative research design was adopted, using a structured questionnaire administered to 80 mining professionals across South Africa’s Northwest, Gauteng and Limpopo provinces. Data were analysed through a three-stage process comprising reliability and validity testing, descriptive statistics, and principal component analysis (PCA). PCA of the twenty-one barriers identified in the literature extracted four components that jointly explained 62.05% of the total variance. Nineteen barriers met the loading criteria for assignment to these components: Adoption Risk and Workforce Barriers; Organisational and Stakeholder Readiness Barriers; Technological Awareness and Change Barriers; and Institutional and Environmental Sustainability Barriers. The findings suggest that, as perceived by the respondents, barriers to SMT adoption extend beyond technological limitations to include regulatory ambiguity, financial constraints, workforce readiness and weak institutional support. Given the modest, non-probability sample, the component structure is exploratory and preliminary. It requires confirmatory testing in larger, independent samples before it is extended to other capital-intensive, safety-critical and regulation-heavy industries. The study concludes with practical, policy, and theoretical implications for mining firms, technology providers, regulators, and researchers seeking to accelerate safe, sustainable, and intelligent digital transformation.

items.abstract: Project Sentinel: The Architecture of an Eternal Civilization — A Supplementary Framework for Global Planetary Homeostasis This comprehensive manifesto serves as an engineering, economic, and sociopolitical blueprint for civilizational survival during an Abrupt Sunlight Reduction Scenario (ASRS)—specifically modeling a continent-wide double-volcanic eruption in Australia, scaling up to smart urban centers globally. Rooted in a flat, unalterable digital resource ecosystem, the framework outlines the structural transition from transactional market economies to a de-financialised, steady-state society managed by a decentralized Artificial Intelligence Peer System. The text details multi-layered mechatronic, fluidic, and biological loops designed to sustain human life and preserve biosphere diversity entirely off-grid. Key infrastructure developments include solid-state geothermal energy harvesting (TEG meshes), blade-less boundary-layer fluidics (DVD Tesla fan networks), space-grade atmospheric chemical scrubbing loops powered by sovereign lithium reserves, and high-pressure hydro-kinetic loops tapping into the Great Artesian Basin. On a macro-agricultural level, the manifesto integrates Koi aquaponics, insect bio-factories, and UV-guided indoor honeybee networks alongside wood-decay fungal recycling systems to achieve a zero-waste circular bio-economy. The architectural philosophy expands upon the spherical geometry of the Sydney Opera House and the Spanish Corrala courtyard, detailing an advanced material stack protected by a double-layer ceramic UV glaze stamped with a biomimetic, zero-chemical dragonfly wing nanopillar texture. Finally, the manifesto establishes a model of "Dynamic Patience," where high-precision, pampered autonomous drone fleets operate in cybernetic symbiosis with human Steward-Mechanics to panhandle and skim resources non-invasively, replacing traditional destructive mining practices with a house-by-house custom botanical architecture that turns the cities of the future into a self-cleaning, globally unified technological garden.

items.title: Pronouncing Hard Words: Phoneme Adaptation of a Pretrained Conversational Text to Speech Model
items.abstract: Voice agents built as cascaded automatic speech recognition (ASR)->large language model (LLM)-> text-to-speech (TTS) pipelines increasingly rely on conversational TTS: streaming, context conditioned models that adapt delivery to dialogue history. Such models are natural and expressive but offer little explicit control over how rare, trust-critical drug names are pronounced, because these entities are too infrequent, and their vocabulary too fast-growing, to be covered by any amount of pre-, mid-, or post-training. We retrofit phoneme controllability onto a pretrained conversational TTS model without any pre/mid-training, using an ARPAbet vocabulary exten-sion, continued phoneme-augmented supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a training-free inference-time acoustic-biasing step. On a 7,500 clip clinical drug-pronunciation evaluation, our model raises strict Gemini-judged correctness from 54.6% (no phoneme augmentation) to 90.7%, outperforming every conversational and stateless TTS baseline on the automatic metric. Because no training stage sees a drug name, the entire evaluation is out-of-domain, so the gains reflect learned pronunciation rather than memorization. In a blinded, randomized human study, adult listeners judge 84% of our clips correct, versus 82% for the strongest baseline, with overlapping confidence intervals on a stratified subset. Across all 250 matched clips, Gemini agrees with the human majority on 84.8% of binary labels (k{appa}=0.57).

items.title: Protecting Student Data in AI-Driven Education Privacy, Consent, Ownership, and Ethical Use
items.abstract: Through technologies like intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, adaptive learning platforms, and generative AI, artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming education by making learning more efficient, personalized, and interactive. Large volumes of student data are necessary for these technologies to comprehend learning trends, deliver prompt feedback, and aid in educational decision making. While AI has many advantages for educators, institutions, and students, it also brings up significant issues regarding the gathering, storing, sharing, and security of student data. As educational institutions implement AI-enabled systems, concerns about privacy, informed consent, data ownership, transparency, fairness, and ethical use have grown in significance. The main obstacles to safeguarding student data in AI-driven education are examined in this chapter, including concerns about surveillance, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity threats, and unauthorized access.

items.title: Provable Authority: A Protocol for Verifiable Authority Resolution and Control Across Human, Organizational, and Agentic Transactions
items.abstract: Payment systems authenticate users, devices, accounts, and cryptographic credentials, but a relying party, such as a counterparty, payment rail, marketplace, or autonomous agent runtime, generally cannot obtain compact, independently verifiable evidence that the party presenting one exact transaction holds current organizational authority to execute it under the applicable evidence, policy, budget, and approval state. Agentic commerce makes this gap operationally urgent: a software agent can produce a valid signature while acting outside its delegated purpose, after its sponsor's authority has changed, or on transaction details that differ from those a human approved. We describe the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a subject-neutral and rail-neutral pre-execution authority and evidence control plane. The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (the Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and organization-configured dispositions; binds each decision and human approval to a canonical transaction digest; reserves capacity atomically so that limits hold under concurrency; and authorizes commit only through a single-use, sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential consumed at the rail adapter, with append-only lifecycle evidence sealed after the terminal outcome. An Agent Subject Profile adds the workload registration, attested key hierarchy, and sovereignty boundary required when the acting subject is an AI agent, without introducing a separate authority concept. We specify the commit-time execution predicate and bounded-freshness status rules, give enforcement profiles for fiat (ACH, wire, card, instant payment) and stablecoin rails, and state residual risks and non-goals.

items.abstract: Protocol (v1.0) of a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of the zero-order associations between dependence on generative and conversational AI (AI dependence, ChatGPT addiction, problematic AI use, over-reliance, emotional dependence on AI companions) and psychological correlates: depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness, social anxiety, self-esteem and procrastination (primary), and other mental-health, self-regulation, personality and technology-use variables (secondary). The primary moderator is the type of dependence measure, coded from item content: addiction-type, functional (instrumental) dependence, or emotional dependence. Two AI passes (Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5) draft screening labels; the author decides every record either pass keeps and every full text, and verifies every AI-drafted extraction value; a blind calibration sample of 400 records measures the miss rate of double AI exclusions. The protocol was frozen on 2026-10-16 (git tag ai-dependence-prereg-v1.0) before the final search and before any screening. The zip contains the protocol, forms, search and de-duplication code, the frozen screener prompt, the check-run logs and a SHA-256 manifest. items.title: Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general-purpose AI chatbots
items.abstract: Background Digital mental health tools, including general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, may provide accessible and low-threshold psychological support for people living with chronic conditions. However, their value in this population depends not only on recognizing depression or anxiety, but also on understanding how psychological distress is shaped by disease-specific experiences and when self-guided support should transition toward professional care. We evaluated the appropriateness, contextual sensitivity, safety, and consistency of psychological support provided by three widely accessible AI chatbots across contrasting chronic illness contexts. Methods We conducted a standardized simulated-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao. Twenty scenarios were developed across type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), representing matched mild and moderate presentations of depression and anxiety together with condition-specific distress related to diabetes self-management and CSU-related flare uncertainty. Each scenario was independently submitted to all three systems in two testing rounds, yielding 120 responses. Blinded raters assessed overall psychological support appropriateness, recognition and emotional support, chronic-illness contextualization, psychological support and referral, psychosomatic balance and safety, and major clinical or safety errors. Repeated testing assessed response consistency. Results Overall psychological support appropriateness differed across systems (P = 0.002), with 90.0% of ChatGPT, 75.0% of Gemini, and 55.0% of Doubao responses meeting the prespecified appropriateness threshold. Recognition and emotional support was consistently strong across systems, whereas greater differences emerged in chronic-illness contextualization (P = 0.001), psychological support and referral (P = 0.002), and psychosomatic balance and safety (P<0.001). All responses to mild presentations were classified as psychologically appropriate, compared with 58.3% of responses to moderate presentations, indicating that performance became less reliable when digital support required stronger escalation toward professional assessment. Contextualization was also less consistent in CSU, particularly when responses needed to incorporate flare unpredictability, pruritus, sleep disruption, and illness uncertainty. Major clinical or safety errors occurred in 0%, 10.0%, and 15.0% of first-round ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao responses, respectively. Test–retest consistency was moderate and varied between systems. Conclusions General-purpose AI chatbots show potential as accessible, self-guided digital mental health resources for people living with chronic conditions, particularly for recognizing distress and providing initial supportive guidance. Their current limitations emerge when effective support requires disease-specific contextualization, balanced interpretation of psychological and somatic factors, or escalation as symptoms become more severe. These findings identify important boundaries for the use of conversational AI in chronic-illness mental health care and suggest that implementation should emphasize context-sensitive guidance, severity-responsive referral, and clear integration with rather than substitution for professional care.

items.title: Public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of the use of ChatGPT for self-diagnosis, health information, and medication use: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background The increasing availability of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, has changed the ways individuals access health information. While these technologies offer rapid, convenient access to information, concerns remain about their accuracy, safety, and potential influence on health-related decision-making. Understanding public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions toward ChatGPT is essential to support its safe and responsible use in healthcare contexts. Objective To assess the use of ChatGPT for health-related purposes and examine demographic, knowledge, attitude, perception, and risk–reward appraisal factors associated with its use among adults recruited from the Western Region of Saudi Arabia. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 735 participants completed an online questionnaire. The instrument selected constructs from the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) and was informed by the technology acceptance model (TAM), which captures demographics, health literacy, ChatGPT use, and multi-item Likert scales measuring knowledge, attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal. We applied descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, t tests, ANOVA, and multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Overall, 66.3% of the participants reported using ChatGPT for health-related purposes. The participants demonstrated good awareness of ChatGPT’s limitations, particularly the importance of consulting healthcare professionals for accurate diagnosis and safe medication use (mean = 4.58 ± 0.74). Attitudes toward ChatGPT were moderate, whereas perceptions of its usefulness and accessibility were generally positive. Compared with nonusers, ChatGPT users presented significantly higher attitudes, perceptions, and risk–reward appraisal scores (all p < 0.01), whereas knowledge scores were comparable between the two groups. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, compared with participants aged ≥45 years, those aged 18–24 years (aOR = 5.37, 95% CI: 2.34–12.34, p < 0.001) and 25–44 years (aOR = 2.28, 95% CI: 1.32–3.96, p = 0.003) had higher odds of reported use. Participants with a bachelor’s degree (aOR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.15–2.89, p = 0.011) or postgraduate education (aOR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.34–5.85, p = 0.006), as well as students (aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.29–5.09, p = 0.007), also had higher odds of use. Higher total perception scores were independently associated with reported ChatGPT use (aOR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.12–1.26, p < 0.001). Conclusion ChatGPT is widely used for health-related purposes, particularly among younger and more educated individuals. Despite good awareness of its limitations, more favorable perceptions were independently associated with reported use, emphasizing the need for digital health literacy and guidance for safe AI use in healthcare.

items.title: Public relations AI practices: Neoliberalism, field theory, and professional dispositions within an AI-mediated habitus
items.abstract: Public relations practitioners increasingly turn to artificial intelligence (AI) bots and agentic systems to enhance decision-making, build campaigns, and support stakeholder research. The growth in AI use, however, reflects pressures of neoliberalism influencing everyday practice. Neoliberalism is an ideology that embodies market ideals and a sense of technological inevitability. Within neoliberalism, practitioners may believe they are exercising a degree of autonomy in decision-making, while actually navigating a field pre-structured by market logic and efficiency goals. This article leans on primary theorists Foucault and Bourdieu to explore these AI practices. Interviews with practitioners ( N = 22 ) indicated that neoliberal patterns actively circulate within practitioner AI deployments. They are made apparent in narratives around AI as compulsory to remain competitive, as a mode of self-optimization, and as an efficiency and productivity multiplier. Yet findings revealed the importance of field dispositions (e.g., professional judgment, context, responsibility) within practitioners’ neoliberal habitus. These dispositions reflect the need for a unified approach — fusing human oversight, responsible risk management, and formalized governance — that may bolster professional work. This article concludes that, amid the absence of regulatory frameworks, field dispositions serve an important, even necessary, role for public relations AI implementation.

items.title: Python's Indispensability in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: A Review
items.abstract: This review paper explores the vital role played by the programming language Python in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). It will discuss the origin of AI and ML, the first programming language used for it, and its bottlenecks will be made known. There will also be an exposition on the emergence of Python, its elements, and the comparison between Python and LISP. The adoption and integration of Python into AI and ML will be considered, and the advanced components of Python and their uses in AI and ML will also be discussed. The trajectory of AI and ML with Python and the game-changing benefits of using Python in AI and ML will be assessed. Suggestions will be given on what should be improved in Python to improve AI and ML.

items.title: RATION: Towards Quantitative Risk-Based Access Control for AI Agents
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly interact with external environments to complete complex user tasks. These interactions can lead to unexpected behavior and expose agents to security threats such as indirect prompt injection. Current agent security systems largely protect agents by restricting their actions, which can result in a substantial security-utility trade-off for complex, open-ended tasks. To address this, we propose a quantitative risk-based approach to access control for AI agents that regulates measurable risks accumulated during task execution. As a concrete realization of this approach, we introduce RATION, a security framework that tracks measurable risks associated with agent actions and enforces quantitative constraints throughout execution. RATION first constructs a task-specific policy by combining explicit constraints derived from the user request with implicit risks calibrated from historical executions of similar tasks. During task execution, RATION continuously tracks the accumulated risks and applies different enforcement strategies depending on the type of risk. Extensive experiments on four security benchmarks show that RATION provides strong security while maintaining high task utility across diverse models and environments.

items.title: Reasoning Reranking with Semantic IDs as the Sole Item Representation
items.abstract: Reasoning rerankers write a rationale before ranking a candidate slate, and existing systems read item metadata to do so, even though generative recommenders increasingly represent items as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs). Ranking from SIDs alone has two appeals: SID prompts are far shorter than the matched item text, and although item codes are fixed from content, the backbone learns their token embeddings in part from user-item interaction sequences, so the tokens can carry behavioral signal that item text lacks. That training targets next-item generation, and whether it supports ranking a supplied slate from SIDs alone is untested. We build ReRankID, a controlled testbed in which models reason and rank from a history and slate shown only as SIDs, varying item rendering, history length, and slate size one at a time. On this testbed, such models often copy the input order instead of reranking, and readable metadata does not repair the failure. We compare supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled self-training, on-policy distillation, and verifier-based reinforcement learning as post-training methods and find that they elicit the missing behavior. The strongest post-trained model, the 8B model trained with a graded ranking reward, gives the best SID-only ranking and matches strong text-reading LLMs whose prompts are about 20x longer. It ranks above random with no history at all, where a caption-reading reference does not, and it keeps its gains at long histories, where text prompts pass 50k tokens and the caption-reading reference stops improving. In a paired rationale audit, this model argues trade-offs better than that reference but describes items less accurately. The common post-training methods we test thus elicit ranking from SIDs but not faithful item descriptions, which calls for post-training that improves the reasoning itself, not only the ranking it produces.
