items.title: Reconfiguration of Skill Requirements in AI-Assisted Software Development: A Criterion for Distinguishing Changes in Requirements from New Task Assignability
items.abstract: When a generative system produces part of the output of a software task, it does not automatically follow that the task can be assigned to people other than those who could perform it without that support. This conceptual study examines the conditions under which delegating only output generation to GenAI changes the skills required of the person to whom the task remains assigned. The method compares two modes of the same task, holding the person, acceptance criteria, quality threshold, and external conditions constant, and draws on the literature on task assignment, human–AI collaboration, and the separation of production and evaluation to delineate the constructs. The result is an identification criterion: new task assignability is attributable to the assisted mode only when the person meets the human skill requirement of the assisted mode but not that of the reference mode. This requires that the capabilities needed to prepare the context, guide generation, and decide whether to accept the output can actually be exercised without an equivalent independent production capability; if this separability does not hold, the production requirement must remain. Three illustrations from software work show how the criterion distinguishes genuinely new task assignability from a reassignment that was already possible or from a change affecting an adjacent activity. The contribution is thus an analytical and verifiable criterion for linking changes in skill requirements to work assignment without conflating generative assistance, task replacement, and agent autonomy.

items.title: Reconstructing Lost Urban Memory with Generative AI: An Oral-History Prompt-Engineering Framework
items.abstract: Urban transformation processes not only destroy the physical fabric of historic neighbourhoods but also erode the collective memory and everyday life practices embedded within them. This study addresses this spatial memory loss by employing generative AI to visually reconstruct the lost atmospheres of Cumhuriyet Neighbourhood within the outer walls of Kayseri Castle, Turkey. Drawing on oral history interviews conducted as part of a TÜBİTAK-funded project, narrative data from 5 former residents were transformed into structured seven-category prompts and fed into Google Gemini- Nano Banana 2 pro, OpenAI GPT-Image-1, and XAI Grok. A 30-member residents panel evaluated the outputs. Tool G (Google Gemini) achieved the best overall ranking (M = 1.77). The findings confirm that human curatorial oversight and iterative community feedback remain essential for culturally authentic AI-generated heritage visualisations.

items.title: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
items.abstract: AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers. As more start collaborating, AI control measures must remain effective when they covertly collude on a harmful objective. We introduce MiniLab, a synthetic series of live services and codebases (5 interconnected services, 249 benign tasks, 8 attack objectives), adapted from internal AI deployment infrastructure. We demonstrate distributed attacks, in which different agents carry out separate attack fragments, and how their covertness evades frontier monitors when reading their trajectories individually. We show how distributed attacks spread across diverse contexts and harmful objectives through 16 human-optimized attacks (weight exfiltration, unmonitored rogue deployment, permission elevation, and more). A frontier monitor, GPT-5.6 Sol, reading each agent separately flags only 7% of successful distributed attacks, compared with 87% when a single agent carries out the same side task. Individual attacks can also be composed into longer attack sequences toward a greater loss-of-control outcome, without any individual agent being flagged. Finally, we tested whether models can plan these covert attacks: even with execution and monitor feedback, the best model-planned attacks succeed covertly against a single-trajectory GPT-5.6 Sol monitor in at most 25% of executions, compared with 80% for human-crafted plans, though this may scale with model capabilities. By turning worst-case coordinated attacks into reproducible red-team cases, our work provides a foundation for preventing locally benign agent actions from accumulating into system-level loss of control.

items.title: Reflect-Guard: Enhancing LLM Safeguards Against Adversarial Prompts via Logical Self-Reflection
items.abstract: LLM safety classifiers such as Llama Guard detect overtly harmful prompts well but remain vulnerable to jailbreaks that disguise intent via role-play, fictional framing, or indirect requests. We present Reflect-Guard: Llama-Guard-3-8B fine-tuned via QLoRA to generate a distilled, GPT-4o-mini-sourced safety rationale before its verdict. Using only 1000training examples and a five-condition ablation, we isolate reflection’s contribution from that of ordinary supervised fine-tuning (SFT). SFT on verdict labels alone already accounts for most of the aggregate gain over the un-fine-tuned baseline (WildGuardTest F1: 0.770 → 0.860; JailbreakBench guard bypass rate: 10.3% → 0.0%). Adding reflection does not improve these aggregate numbers further (F1 falls to 0.842, guard bypass rises to 1.8%) but reallocates performance toward adversarially framed inputs: adversarial-subset recall rises from 0.845 (SFT-only) to 0.921 (+7.6 pp), at a cost of −7.9 pp precision on that subset. The same direction holds across three training seeds (paired t-tests, p=0.018 for overall F1 and p=0.027 for adversarial recall), though we interpret these values cautiously given the small number of seeds. Measured inference latency is 17.9× the baseline’s, driven by ∼92 additional reflection tokens per prompt. The same checkpoint, without additional fine-tuning, shows promising zero-shot transfer to a 329-example financial-harm benchmark (F1: 0.868 → 0.929; recall: 0.767 → 0.867, zero false positives); preliminary two-seed evidence, however, suggests the SFT-only condition may match or exceed this result, so we treat the finance improvement as evidence toward generalization rather than a settled advantage of reflection specifically. Benchmarked against WildGuard, PromptGuard, and a prompted (non-fine-tuned) GPT-4o-mini reasoning classifier on the same sets, WildGuard leads on aggregate WildGuardTest F1 (0.887), while Reflect-Guard achieves higher adversarial-subset recall than every evaluated classifier, including WildGuard (0.921 vs. 0.827) and the prompted teacher (0.636). Overall, supervised fine-tuning drives most of the aggregate gain over an un-fine-tuned classifier, while the generated safety rationale yields a narrower, latency-costly improvement specifically in adversarial-subset recall, a precision–recall tradeoff relevant to safety-critical deployments that prioritize recall over inference speed.

items.title: Reframing education 5.0 through capability theory: A framework for human-centered digital learning
items.abstract: Industry 5.0 has reoriented technology-driven transformation around human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience, complementing rather than replacing Industry 4.0, with direct implications for education. Existing accounts of the resulting “Education 5.0” paradigm remain largely descriptive, synthesising a dispersed literature without an explicit theoretical mechanism or a transparent, auditable procedure for deriving the constructs they propose. This paper addresses both gaps. First, it anchors the Education 4.0-to-5.0 transition within the capability approach, using capability expansion, not technology adoption, as the mechanism linking Industry 5.0’s human-centric, sustainable, and resilient logic to curricular practice, and specifies the boundary conditions under which the framework should, and should not, be expected to hold. Second, it derives an integrative five-pillar curriculum framework - human-centric pedagogy, resilient and lifelong learning ecosystems, sustainability-embedded curricula, well-being and leadership development, and creativity through human–AI co-creation - through an explicit three-step synthesis procedure that traces each pillar to recurring literature constructs, reported as an auditable construct crosswalk rather than asserted as self-evident. Third, it formalises the framework as a computable model: an Education 5.0 Readiness Index (ER5.0I), built from Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pillar weights, and an Industry 5.0–Education 5.0 Alignment Coefficient (IEAC), computed as cosine similarity between pillar-emphasis vectors. All numeric weights and scores are explicitly labelled as illustrative placeholders demonstrating the model’s mechanics, not empirical findings; the paper specifies the Delphi/AHP expert-panel protocol, a candidate measurement instrument, a single-institution pilot case study, and the psychometric (CFA/SEM) validation route required before the framework can be treated as measurement rather than illustration. items.title: Regulating the Digital Divide: Policy Interventions for Equitable Access to AI-Enabled E-Learning Platforms
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming global education systems, offering unprecedented opportunities for personalization, efficiency, and adaptive learning. However, the integration of AI in education has also deepened existing digital divides, particularly in under-resourced communities lacking adequate infrastructure, policy support, and inclusive design. This study proposes the Equity-Centered AI Learning Access Model (ECALAM)—a conceptual framework developed through a qualitative synthesis of recent literature and policy reports—to understand and address systemic barriers to equitable AI adoption. ECALAM identifies four interrelated domains: structural inequities, AI accessibility challenges, inclusive design adaptation, and policy governance. Findings indicate that AI-enhanced learning systems, when deployed without attention to algorithmic fairness, linguistic diversity, and access equity, risk reinforcing educational stratification. Inclusive design principles, adaptive technologies, and regulatory frameworks are shown to play a pivotal role in enabling just and accessible learning environments. The study concludes with policy recommendations for governments, educators, and technology developers, emphasizing the need for anticipatory governance and inclusive pedagogical integration. ECALAM offers a diagnostic and strategic tool for guiding ethical and equitable AI implementation in education, particularly across diverse and underserved global contexts.

items.title: Rehabilitation and Modernization of the Kaduna Polytechnic Central Library and Ungwan Rimi Campus Library
items.abstract: Executive Overview This document presents an independent institutional infrastructure proposal titled "Rehabilitation and Modernization of the Kaduna Polytechnic Central Library and Ungwan Rimi Campus Library," developed as a turnkey capital intervention model for Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria. Designed to address physical decay, structural leaks, and technological obsolescence within the institution's primary knowledge repository, this proposal establishes a comprehensive framework for transforming the Central Library and Ungwan Rimi Campus Library into a modern, resilient, and digitally integrated research hub. Technical Scope & Library Modernization Pillars The proposed intervention covers four core structural and academic pillars: 1. Civil & Environmental Rehabilitation: Complete roof leak remediation, structural ceiling repairs, climate control restoration, and lighting upgrades to protect collections and create a conducive study environment. 2. Digital Repository & ICT Integration: Procurement and installation of computer search terminals, high-speed network connectivity, and digital cataloging software (e.g., Koha / DSpace) to connect students and faculty with global e-resources. 3. Ergonomic Study Spaces & Capacity Expansion: Overhaul of reading tables, ergonomic seating, and individual study carrels to expand comfortable seating capacity for researchers. 4. Collection Preservation & Information Literacy: Implementation of humidity-controlled archival storage, preservation protocols for rare technical volumes, and digital literacy training frameworks for academic staff and library personnel. Financial Framework & Project Metrics · Proposed Beneficiary Institution: Kaduna Polytechnic, Kaduna State, Nigeria · Target Supervising Units: Central Library Services & Directorate of Works and Physical Planning · Implementation Duration: 6 Months · Total Estimated Budget: ₦120,000,000 (approx. $75,000 USD equivalent) · Target Funding Mechanism: The Elsevier Foundation Purpose & Open-Access Availability This document is published on Zenodo as an open-access policy and educational infrastructure artifact. It serves as an actionable benchmark for university librarians, academic administrators, educational policy researchers, and philanthropic foundations seeking structured models for academic library modernization in developing nations.

items.title: Reimagining Education: The Transformative Power of Artificial Intelligence in Shaping Future Learning
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) begins to shake the world of education by providing new solutions that can enhance its achievement and the quality of instruction. In this paper, artificial intelligence in the education field is discussed according to its applications, issues, and prospects by way of a methodical literature review, which reveals some valuable information on the use of AI technology in learning processes. The findings show that data analytics applications, adaptive teaching systems, and AI-based personalized learning platforms allow personalized teaching, learned information, and improved collaboration. The practicality of AI in education is severely hindered by the fear of algorithmic bias and data privacy, as well as transparency. The results suggest that ethical AI practices and cooperation are required to make the digital technology era equitable and successful within the context of both accessibility and student success. They also refer to the possibility of AI transformation of education that can equalize, inclusivity, and productiveness of learning environments to all learners.

items.title: Reporting-lag-aware machine learning framework for short-term forecasting of respiratory disease activity: a sentinel hospital study in Guangzhou
items.abstract: Abstract Background Reporting delays in laboratory confirmation constrain timely situational awareness in respiratory disease surveillance. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a reporting-lag-aware machine learning framework for short-term, age-stratified forecasting of respiratory disease activity under real-world surveillance constraints. Methods We analyzed 1004 days (November 1, 2023 to July 31, 2026) of surveillance data from a national sentinel hospital in Guangzhou, China, including physician-recorded or laboratory-supported influenza, COVID-19 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae cases, fever clinic visits and meteorological variables. Given a routine 2-day reporting lag, an XGBoost model predicted the 7-day-ahead case increment. Most count-derived predictors were normalized, while the latest observable case count was retained as a level anchor. The shrinkage-calibrated XGBoost forecast was combined with a rolling SARIMA forecast. Comparators included naive rules, SARIMA, an oracle-weather SARIMAX benchmark, LSTM and Transformer models. Performance was assessed using RMSE, MAE, R 2 , directional accuracy, alert sensitivity, positive predictive value and prediction-interval coverage over 363 scored target dates within a 371-day calendar evaluation window. Results The framework achieved RMSE values of 16.50, 12.64 and 6.14 in the total population, adults and children, respectively, with corresponding R 2 values of 0.640, 0.694 and 0.353. It significantly outperformed persistence in the total and adult series (Diebold-Mariano p = 0.001 and 0.003), but improvements over a 7-day moving average or rolling SARIMA were not statistically significant. No comparison was statistically significant in children. For the proposed framework, directional accuracy was 67.2% to 73.5%, and sensitivity for identifying days on which activity reached or exceeded twice the development-period median was 58.1% to 78.4%. The absolute-count specification performed worse over the extended evaluation period (RMSE = 20.32; R 2 = 0.453), during which fever clinic attendance declined by 31.5% and the case-to-visit ratio increased by 31.6%. Conclusions A reporting-lag-aware framework based on routine data provided modest supplementary 7-day situational awareness. Its improvement over persistence was approximately one case per day in MAE, with no significant advantage over a 7-day moving average or rolling SARIMA. Performance depended on the stability of count-based predictors under shifts in care-seeking behaviour, supporting prospective multi-site validation before broader use.

items.title: Research on the construction of an adaptive mindfulness-based cognitive therapy system based on large language models and its efficacy in addressing college students’ anxiety
items.abstract: To handle the problem of resource scarcity and lack of personalization and adaptability in the traditional approach to mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) in dealing with college students with anxiety disorders, this study proposes the use of the natural language interface and adaptability properties of large language models (LLMs) to come up with an intelligent college-level MBCT intervention system. To begin with, the system functional requirements and the logic of the system intervention were explained in line with the fundamental ideas of MBCT and the cognitive features of students with anxiety. Second, it was created through a four-stage adaptive architecture that includes perception analysis, intervention, and feedback, providing a dynamic process for user status identification, personal generation of intervention plans, and real-time optimization of the intervention process. Finally, there was a randomized controlled trial whose subjects were 120 college students with anxiety who were separated into an experimental group and a control group. The effectiveness of the intervention was assessed using tools such as the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS), and the Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire (ATQ). The findings indicated that the SAS score of the experimental group (38.26 ± 5.12) was significantly less than that of the control group (45.89 ± 6.34), the MAAS score (68.73 ± 7.25) was significantly higher than that of the control group (56.41 ± 8.13); and the ATQ score (42.15 ± 6.08) was significantly less than that of the control group. The study reveals that an adaptive MBCT system using large language models may be effective in reducing anxiety symptoms among college students, improving mindfulness, and enhancing cognitive processes, offering a new, readily available strategy for addressing anxiety in college students.

items.title: Resisting AI with Paper: Possibilities, Concerns and Protest
items.abstract: While there are a number of commercial benefits involved in incorporating AI usage and training into college composition classrooms, to many the perils and problems involved in student AI use outweigh these possibilities. A growing number of composition instructors have chosen to return to requiring assignments to be handwritten on paper as an increasingly viable, and even necessary, strategy to combat the growing use of ChatGPT and other AI text generation software as an essay-writing tool. This strategy has a number of potential benefits – the ability to regulate AI usage, to create better memory retention, and decrease student screen-time – but there are also many potential drawbacks. This panel aims to discuss the viability and sustainability of this option in the AI debate, with special attention to the environmental costs of paper vs. AI, the practicality of implementing paper assignments, and overall where the instructor’s priorities in the modern college composition classroom should lie. The debate might ultimately come down to whether in training for AI usage in the workplace or focusing on the retention of composition skills should be the modern priority. Overall, the question of whether the paper option is a viable solution is a somewhat underdiscussed topic in the AI debate, and this panel aims to consider thoughts from college instructors on the pros and cons thereof.

items.title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence and Ethical Data Governance
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming education by supporting personalized learning, intelligent decision-making and data-driven practices. As AI becomes more integrated into teaching, learning, assessment and institutional management, the ethical use of educational data has become increasingly important. This chapter examines responsible AI and ethical data governance in education. It discusses AI applications such as intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning and learning analytics together with the opportunities and challenges they present. The chapter explores the educational data ecosystem, including data sources, governance, ownership and ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy and explainability. It also examines responsible data management, informed consent, data security and approaches to reducing algorithmic bias. Emerging issues including student surveillance, online proctoring, generative AI, academic integrity, learner autonomy and well-being are discussed.

items.abstract: Purpose: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has entered university teaching in Bangladesh faster than institutional rules. This paper asks which risks require institutional control when GenAI is used in teaching and assessment, and which governance design can allow proportionate use while protecting learning, integrity, privacy, fairness and human accountability.Design/methodology/approach: The study is a structured integrative review and normative policy analysis of 61 sources: peer-reviewed research on GenAI in higher education, academic integrity, assessment design and AI literacy; Bangladeshi empirical studies; and international and national policy instruments, including Bangladesh’s draft National AI Policy 2026–2030. Sources were coded against five governance domains and interpreted through three lenses: assessment validity, rights-based responsible AI and virtue ethics.Findings: Prohibition is hard to enforce and can widen inequity, while unrestricted adoption shifts educational judgment to opaque commercial systems. Bangladeshi evidence shows near-universal reliance on free tool versions, weak institutional guidance, unreliable Bangla-language output and uneven device and connectivity access.Originality/value: The paper proposes a five-domain (access, assessment, data, authorship, accountability), three-tier (prohibited, supervised, permitted assisted) framework and a five-step assessment assurance cycle that treats assessment validity, rather than detection, as the central object of governance.Implications: The framework gives universities and the University Grants Commission a low-cost route from broad AI principles to course-level permissions, process evidence, oral verification and appeal. It is a conceptual proposal that requires empirical piloting.

items.title: ResQAI – Intelligent Emergency Resource Allocation and Crisis Response Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: During an emergency, getting the right help at the right time is very important. However, many existing emergencyreporting methods mainly depend on manual communication, which can cause delays in identifying the type and severity of an emergency and assigning suitable resources. This paper presents ResQAI, an intelligent emergency response application designed to improve the process of reporting, analyzing, and responding to emergency situations.ResQAI uses artificial intelligence to identify the emergency category from the user's description and predict its severity. Based on the emergency type, severity, location, and availability of resources, the system helps assign suitable resources and volunteers. The application also uses GPS to capture the emergency location and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to send notifications to the concerned users and organizations. A voice-based reporting option allows users to describe an emergency using speech, which is converted into text before submitting the report. To support situations where internet connectivity is unavailable, ResQAI stores emergency requests locally using SQLite and synchronizes them with the server when connectivity is restored. The proposed approach combines artificial intelligence, location services, mobile technology, and offline synchronization in a single emergency response platform. The system is intended to reduce manual effort, improve response coordination, and provide a more organized approach to emergency resource allocation.

items.title: Review of Health Knowledge Graphs for Clinical Decision Support: Construction, LLM-Grounded Reasoning, and Applications
items.abstract: Health Knowledge Graphs (Health-KGs) structure heterogeneous medical information from Electronic Health Records (EHRs), the biomedical literature, and clinical guidelines into machine-reasonable form, and have become a foundation for clinical decision support. This work reviews the construction and application of Health-KGs following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, organizing the literature along three axes representation, extraction, and integration and situating it against prior biomedical-KG reviews. We examine knowledge-representation learning and graph-embedding models, named-entity recognition, disambiguation, and linking, and cross-source integration, together with the principal EHR datasets and clinical language models that underpin them. A distinguishing focus is the shift toward large language models (LLMs): we synthesize LLM-driven entity and relation extraction, retrieval and graph-augmented clinical reasoning, and the factuality and hallucination constraints that govern their safe use an axis not addressed by prior EHR-focused reviews. We further reviewed applications spanning drug development and clinical trials, diagnosis and prediction, treatment recommendation, question answering, and health-policy compliance. Finally, we identify the central open challenges: the absence of a standardized, openly governed Health-KG benchmark; heterogeneous and temporally evolving clinical data; multimodal fusion; and privacy-preserving, reproducible construction. This review is intended as a roadmap for data scientists, medical-informatics and AI researchers, and healthcare practitioners.

items.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
items.abstract: Time-aware retrieval is crucial for long-horizon LLM agents to effectively leverage ever-growing long-term memory. Existing methods focus on lexical or semantic similarity, leading to target memories being crowded out by temporally mismatched yet semantically similar candidates. Even time-aware approaches inject temporal cues only during memory organization or answer generation, overlooking temporal constraints at the retrieval stage, where candidate selection occurs - the root cause of the displacement. Inspired by the temporal contiguity effect in human episodic memory, we propose TIDER (Temporal Interval-driven Dual-channel Evidence Retrieval), a time-aware agentic retrieval framework. Central to TIDER is a reinforcement learning (RL)-trained temporal interval locator that infers the temporal windows in which the evidence lies. RL optimizes window localization as a discrete, non-differentiable retrieval decision, using composite rewards to convert sparse answer supervision into fine-grained retrieval feedback. These temporal windows first define the temporal retrieval channel; the retrieved candidates are then merged with results from the semantic channel and reranked by proximity to the windows. This temporal grounding enables TIDER to retrieve temporally aligned evidence that would otherwise be drowned out by the volume of semantically similar yet temporally mismatched memories. With a lightweight 1.7B locator, TIDER achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on both long-horizon memory benchmarks - 61.52% on LifeBench (+8.82%) and 78.96% on LoCoMo (+3.66%) - which indicates that temporal cues are crucial for pinpointing target evidence amid a vast pool of semantically similar historical events in long-term daily-life memory.

items.title: Robot-assisted cognitive assessment with eye-tracking
items.abstract: Most robot-assisted cognitive and mental health assessments have relied on self-report questionnaires or standardized cognitive tests. Although these tools yield useful summary scores, they may miss subtle, continuous changes in attention, visuomotor control, and memory. Eye-tracking tasks, such as smooth pursuit and visuospatial memory (VisMET), can provide continuous measures of cognitive and oculomotor processes. Previous studies have compared robot- and human-assisted conventional cognitive assessments, but matched comparisons of robot- and human-assisted eye-tracking workflows remain scarce. Here, we directly compared robot-assisted and human-assisted eye-tracking assessment workflows using the same eye-tracker model and matched procedures. Administrators completed both conditions in a within-subjects design, whereas recipients were assigned to one condition and completed the smooth pursuit and VisMET tasks. Dependent measures included velocity gain and root mean square error for smooth pursuit, and valid gaze sample, fixation, saccade, and area-of-interest measures for VisMET. Recipients and administrators also rated usability, perceived workload, and trust using the SUS, NASA-TLX, and SSRIT. We did not detect statistically significant between-condition differences in eye-movement or user-experience measures among assessment recipients (all FDR-corrected ps ≥ 0.128). Administrators reported lower NASA-TLX scores in the robot-assisted condition than in the human-assisted condition (25.67 vs. 37.16; FDR-corrected p = 0.081, Cohen's dz = −0.50), and usability and trust ratings were similar across conditions. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the technical and workflow feasibility of robot-assisted eye-tracking assessment and support further evaluation in broader, clinically relevant populations.

items.title: Robust Tool Selection Beyond Description Matching
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents choose which external tool to call from the tools' documentation, and this description matching fails in three measurable ways: similar tools create ambiguity, truncated or anonymized documentation creates degradation, and untrusted catalogs admit adversarial injection. We present Three-Axis Tool Selection (TATS), which answers each condition with a different signal: a contextual bandit that learns online to separate similar tools, schema features that survive the loss of descriptions, and a success-filtered anomaly penalty (ADAB) that downweights candidates unlike anything that has succeeded before. All three run inside one compact eight-feature selector with no LLM call at inference, evaluated axis by axis on BFCL and MetaTool. Under ambiguity, TATS's advantage over description matching widens from 12.6 to 21.4 points as similar candidates grow from 5 to 50; under name-only documentation, schema features keep 62.1% accuracy where description matching falls to 30.2%; under injection, ADAB cuts the selection rate of a malicious tool from 6.9% to 1.7% at a 3.4-point clean-catalog cost. We state when any feature-only defense cannot stop an attacker who knows the scoring rule, confirm it with a relaxed oracle, and show that an unforgeable registry of trusted tools reduces the same attack to about 1% of queries.

items.title: Rockets, Thrusters, Capsules and Spacesuits
items.abstract: Chapter 3 introduces ‘the Big Four’—rockets, thrusters, capsules and spacesuits—that are the essential elements for getting into space, travelling and manoeuvring in space and being protected from the lethal environment of space, when inside and outside a spacecraft. Following a description of Earth’s atmosphere, the space environment and its hazards are described. Rocket principles and a basic outline of orbital mechanics and spaceflight are presented, including circular and non-circular orbits, orbital transfers, changing speed and direction in space and trajectories from Earth to the Moon. Next follows a description of space capsules, their function and role in protecting astronauts, followed by a detailed discussion of spacesuits and the ergonomics of their role as protective clothing in the environment of space including the lunar surface.

items.title: safety culture assessment based on the Hearts and Minds methodology: maturity analysis in a railway sector company
items.abstract: Large-scale industrial accidents in recent decades have demonstrated that, beyond technical failures, human and organizational factors play a central role in the occurrence of critical events. In Brazil, organizational safety culture has become a key pillar of accident prevention, particularly in high-risk sectors such as the railway industry. Against this backdrop, this study aims to assess organizational safety culture using the "Hearts and Minds" methodology, developed by Shell and disseminated by the Energy Institute. The research is descriptive and exploratory in nature, employing specific tools from the methodology to analyze safety-related perceptions, attitudes, and behaviors, as well as to determine the organizational culture's maturity level. The analysis seeks to diagnose the current state of the safety culture and highlight factors influencing Occupational Health and Safety performance, with a particular focus on leadership commitment and employee engagement. The findings are expected to contribute to the advancement of safety culture maturity, thereby fostering risk reduction and strengthening preventive practices within the railway environment.

items.title: Same basis, not a lower bar: design of SameBasis, a teacher-controlled AI decision-support prototype for reasonable adjustments in Australian schools
items.abstract: In 2025, 27.0% of Australian school students received an educational adjustment due to disability. Under the Disability Standards for Education 2005, each adjustment must let the student take part on the same basis as their peers, yet the 2020 Review of the Standards found that many educators struggle to know how. This design report presents SameBasis, a web-based prototype in which generative AI drafts one specific, reasoned adjustment for a named student in a named activity, covering UDL, cultural and trauma-informed reasoning. The teacher always decides, implemented adjustments become NCCD-ready evidence, and an equity monitor makes AI use visible to the school. The paper sets out six design principles, maps features to obligations, states limitations plainly (synthetic data only, not yet evaluated, not a compliance tool) and proposes a staged evaluation plan. items.title: SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture
items.abstract: SAP AI Core provides enterprise capabilities for executing, managing, and operationalizing Artificial Intelligence workloads within SAP Business Technology Platform landscapes. Enterprise adoption requires a reference architecture that connects model runtime, data, applications, identity, security, integration, observability, Responsible AI, and lifecycle governance. This paper proposes a SAP AI Core Enterprise Reference Architecture spanning user and application channels, AI service orchestration, model runtime, data and feature access, SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Datasphere, SAP Integration Suite, model repositories, security controls, monitoring, and governance. The architecture supports predictive AI, custom machine learning, Generative AI, embeddings, and agentic services while maintaining clean-core integration, least privilege, auditability, resilience, and business accountability. It also defines implementation patterns, deployment controls, model lifecycle processes, and operational KPIs/KRIs. The proposed architecture enables organizations to scale AI on SAP BTP in a secure, reusable, and governed manner.

items.abstract: SAP Joule introduces a generative AI copilot experience across SAP applications and enterprise workflows. Successful enterprise adoption requires more than technical enablement because organizations must align business use cases, process ownership, data readiness, identity, security, Responsible AI, change management, and measurable value. This paper proposes a SAP Joule Enterprise Adoption Framework that guides organizations from strategy and use-case prioritization through architecture, integration, governance, pilot execution, scale-out, monitoring, and continuous improvement. items.title: Scheduled service network design: From classical models to intelligent, data-driven, and cyber–physical networks
items.abstract: Scheduled Service Network Design (SSND) focuses on tactical planning in freight and passenger transportation systems, especially across rail, air, and maritime logistics. The SSND determines the optimal demand itineraries by selecting a set of scheduled services connecting origin, transfer, and destination terminals. This paper presents a unified review of the SSND literature, where different generic types of the SSND in freight and passenger transportation systems are first defined and formulated. Subsequently, 106 relevant journal papers published between January 2008 and June 2026 were systematically collected and analyzed. To gain a deeper understanding of the SSND research landscape, a bibliometric analysis was conducted using VOSviewer software to map key authors, leading countries, and research trends. These studies are classified according to their objectives, underlying assumptions, and network design frameworks, enabling the identification of major trends and research gaps. Particular attention is given to recent advancements, with emphasis on emerging research directions such as demand selection, synchronization, flexible SSND, multi-tier SSND, disruption scenarios, and capacity configurations. Extending beyond traditional optimization-based SSND, this survey investigates the emerging paradigm of intelligent, data-driven, and cyber–physical network design. It reviews how the integration of Internet of Things (IoT), machine learning, reinforcement learning, digital twins, and cyber–physical systems is reshaping SSND through enhanced situational awareness, predictive decision-making, and adaptive network operations. This review serves as a valuable resource for both researchers and practitioners by offering a clear overview of the current state of SSND research and providing actionable guidance for advancing tactical planning in next-generation SSNDs.

items.title: Schizophrenia research in 2026: report from the annual meeting of the Schizophrenia International Research Society
items.abstract: Abstract SIRS 2026, held under the theme “Schizophrenia Research in the Era of Artificial Intelligence,” brought together researchers, clinicians, and persons with lived experience to take stock of a field whose tools for measuring, predicting, and intervening in psychosis have expanded rapidly. Themes spanned artificial intelligence, automated speech analysis, retinal imaging, computational modelling, and novel psychosocial and pharmacological targets, with evidence that, individually, warrants cautious but serious attention and that, collectively, points toward a more mechanistically grounded psychiatry. A recurring call across the meeting was for rigorous external validation, equitable implementation, and sustained scrutiny of underlying assumptions, including whether existing diagnostic categories and treatment targets remain adequate. Some areas remained underworked relative to their importance, including translating basic neuroscience advances into questions relevant to patients and families, and the structural determinants of illness onset and treatment access. Perhaps the most significant development at SIRS 2026 was not any single scientific finding but the broadening of whose voices and experiences are treated as evidence worth taking seriously in this era of AI, a shift whose consolidation remains a question for the field as much as for any individual programme of work.

items.title: ScholarForge AI: An Open, Multi-Agent RAG Platform for Automated Research Paper Analysis
items.abstract: The growing volume of scientific literature has made research-paper analysis increasingly time-consuming for students, researchers, and academicians. Tasks such as literature review generation, methodology understanding, research gap identification, citation formatting, and trend discovery often require substantial manual effort. To address these challenges, this paper presents ScholarForge AI, an open, multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform designed to automate research-paper analysis and transform scholarly documents into actionable research intelligence. The proposed system integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestration, ChromaDB vector storage, a Neo4j knowledge graph, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to support intelligent document processing. Research papers in PDF format are processed using PyMuPDF and EasyOCR, then chunked and embedded with the BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 sentence transformer model for semantic retrieval. The platform includes specialized agents for literature review generation, methodology analysis, research gap detection, trend analysis, research idea generation, citation formatting, interactive question answering and difficulty prediction. In addition, a research difficulty predictor classifies papers as Easy, Medium, or Hard, while the knowledge graph visualizes relationships among papers, authors, keywords, methods, and topics. Experimental results show that ScholarForge AI improves the efficiency of literature survey preparation, supports accurate gap identification, and provides context-aware research recommendations. Built entirely on open-source technologies, the platform offers a scalable and accessible solution for academic research support.

items.title: Science of Vocating in Organisations
items.abstract: Chapter 2 establishes that organisational vocation is grounded not only in philosophy or lived experience, but in a broad and rigorous scientific foundation. Drawing on neuroscience, psychology, organisational identity theory, stakeholder science, systems thinking, behavioural economics, impact measurement, global development frameworks and AI governance, it argues that purpose is a structural force shaping motivation, resilience, trust, cooperation and institutional effectiveness. The chapter shows that organisations flourish when their identity, culture, leadership, systems and accountability mechanisms align with human dignity, shared meaning and measurable impact. It further contends that the rise of artificial intelligence intensifies the urgency of vocational coherence: in an era where algorithms increasingly shape decisions, organisations must ensure that technology serves human agency rather than eroding it. Vocation therefore becomes not merely an inward reflection, but a design discipline guiding governance, incentives, measurement and digital architecture. By integrating scientific evidence with practical insight, Chapter 2 provides the intellectual and ethical foundation for the Seven-Step Vocating Framework that follows, positioning organisational vocation as a credible, evidence-based pathway for building institutions that are resilient, human-centred and fit for the age of AI.

items.title: Secure Design Principles for AI-Driven Learning Platforms
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into educational tools such as learning management systems, analytics dashboards, adaptive assessment services, and generative AI assistants. These platforms support personalized learning and institutional decision-making, but they create risks linked to digital identity, learner profiling, data misuse, model leakage, prompt injection, and weak governance. This chapter analyzes cybersecurity governance in AI-driven learning platforms from the perspective of identity security and data privacy. It examines AI-specific privacy threats and safeguards such as zero trust, decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, encryption, federated learning, differential privacy, secure aggregation, and accountable oversight. The chapter proposes a layered cybersecurity framework integrating identity assurance, privacy-preserving processing, AI model protection, secure platform operations, institutional governance, and continuous risk monitoring. The contribution supports trustworthy, privacy-aware, and secure AI-enabled education ecosystems.

items.title: Self-Building Labs
items.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still takes extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting the role of human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

items.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness. In light of this, we propose Self-HPO, a recursive self-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates (H-step). The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning (RL) under the selected harness (P-step), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy's evolving failure modes. Across three coding benchmarks, Self-HPO consistently outperforms harness-only and policy-only baselines, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%, with gains generalizing to out-of-distribution settings. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains. Self-HPO also improves reliability (Pass@1) and expands the capability frontier (Pass@k) over the base agent. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model (e.g., Opus 4.8) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost.

items.title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent outputs that lack source support or conflict with local operational constraints. We introduce Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a modular architecture that organizes generation as a closed Retrieve--Reflect--Revise loop. SRCoT separates environment state, persistent knowledge, accumulated experience, and short-term memory into provenance-labeled stores. BM25 retrieval supplies local context; subsequent passes expose intermediate drafts, missing-information markers, follow-up queries, and optional claim--evidence mappings. These artifacts inform retrieval, revision, clarification, or abstention decisions. We examine the architecture through qualitative, trace-based case studies in two fully synthetic settings: emergency medical services and Munich-Sim, an emergency-operations simulation. Local prototype runs on an Apple M4-family laptop with 128 GB memory illustrate source-labeled documentation, explicit gap marking, and structured dispatch-style outputs. The traces also reveal provenance-assignment errors, incomplete evidence coverage, and unsafe assumptions that remain possible despite prompting constraints. These cases demonstrate report-level inspectability and local execution, not comparative superiority, hallucination reduction, clinical validity, or operational safety. The architecture separates retrieval and control from the model interface, but behavior across different models remains to be evaluated. SRCoT is a research proof of concept requiring human review, with its principal contribution lying in an inspectable control procedure rather than a new model.

items.title: Seven-Step Vocating Framework for Organisations
items.abstract: Chapter 3 translates the concept of organisational vocation into a practical seven-step framework for enterprise design, leadership and governance. Moving from theory to implementation, it presents vocating as a structured yet iterative process through which organisations align purpose with culture, strategy, stakeholder relationships, resilience, measurable impact and technological responsibility. The framework begins by helping organisations rediscover their passion and dream, then guides them to define a credible Theory of Change, identify the communities they are truly called to serve, and craft a vision and path capable of shaping daily behaviour and long-term direction. It further shows how crises can become catalysts for growth, how outward-facing ambition can shift the focus from self-preservation to stakeholder flourishing, and how rigorous measurement and verification transform aspiration into accountability. Throughout, the chapter emphasises that, in the age of artificial intelligence, vocation must also govern systems design: technology should amplify human agency, dignity and trust rather than accelerate drift, opacity or extraction. The Seven-Step Vocating Framework is thus presented not merely as a leadership model, but as an organisational architecture for building resilient, human-centred and impact-driven enterprises in a rapidly changing world.

items.title: Shame and Release Scale (SRS): A PRISMA Systematic Literature Review and Multi-Domain Psychometric Instrument Development Rationale for Indian Organisational Contexts
items.abstract: Background Shame is a universal emotion with profound implications for mental health, workplace functioning, and social cohesion, yet its measurement remains critically underdeveloped in South Asian organizational contexts. Despite the global burden of unmeasured shame in organizational and development settings, no validated Hindi or Indian general shame instruments have been reported in the literature. This gap is particularly acute in workplace shame measurement for South Asian populations, where culturally specific constructs such as sharam (shame), izzat (honour), and lajja (shame/modesty) shape emotional experience in ways not captured by Western instruments [5]. Furthermore, no existing shame instrument combines the measurement of shame (wound) with release (healing), leaving a critical void in understanding pathways from shame to recovery. The absence of instruments addressing structural shame rooted in colonial trauma and caste hierarchies, as discussed in diaspora contexts [8], further limits the capacity to measure and address inherited shame in Indian organizational contexts. Methods A comprehensive systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed across SciSpace, Google Scholar, and PubMed for peer-reviewed literature published between 2000 and 2026. A two-stage LLM-based screening process was employed with a relevance threshold of 3.0/5.0, focusing on eligibility criteria that addressed shame constructs, cultural context, psychometric evaluation, workplace dynamics, and therapeutic processes. Studies were included if they reported on shame measurement instruments, cultural manifestations of shame in South Asian or collectivist contexts, workplace shame dynamics, structural or inherited shame, or shame release interventions. Results The search identified 3,479 records, of which 479 duplicates were removed. A total of 3,000 records were screened, 216 records were assessed for eligibility (2 in full text, 214 on title, abstract and metadata), and 205 studies were included in the final synthesis. Key evidence domains included psychometric instruments such as the External and Internal Shame Scale (EISS) [3], Other as Shamer Scale (OAS) [11], Test of Self-Conscious Affect-3 (TOSCA-3), Internalized Shame Scale (ISS) [10], Guilt and Shame Proneness Scale (GASP) [12], and culturally specific scales including the Interpersonal Shame Inventory for Asian Americans [13] and the Crime-Related Shame and Guilt Scale for Philippine prisoners [1]. Evidence on cultural manifestations of shame in South Asian contexts highlighted the role of honour-shame dynamics [5], caste-based intergenerational trauma [8], and silence as both defense and survival in collectivist societies [2]. Workplace shame dynamics were documented across healthcare [6], fast food industry crises [7], and academic settings [9], with findings on collective shame, turnover intentions, and organizational dehumanization. Limited evidence was found on structural shame rooted in colonial and caste systems, though qualitative work has explored politicizing pain and caste-based trauma [4] [8], and shame release interventions remained underexplored in organizational contexts. Conclusions Critical gaps persist in culturally adapted shame measurement for South Asian populations, particularly the absence of validated Hindi instruments and tools addressing structural shame rooted in colonial trauma and caste hierarchies. No existing instrument combines shame and release dimensions, limiting the capacity to measure pathways from shame to healing in organizational settings. The development of the Shame and Release Scale (SRS) addresses these gaps by integrating culturally salient shame constructs with a release subscale, offering a novel psychometric tool for Indian organizational contexts. Future validation efforts must prioritize community engagement, cultural adaptation, and rigorous psychometric evaluation to ensure the SRS meets the needs of South Asian populations.

items.title: SimpleVLN: Towards Simple and Frontier Vision-Language Navigation
items.abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to ground language in visual observations and make long-horizon decisions. Existing methods often address these demands through task-specific architectures. As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly capable, an important question remains: Have we truly unlocked the potential of native MLLMs for VLN before introducing task-specific architecture? We present SimpleVLN, an architecture-preserving framework developed through studies of navigation formulation, data construction, and optimization. At the formulation level, SimpleVLN combines single-turn decision inputs with fixed-budget global-local memory to efficiently use navigation history without unbounded context growth, while action chunks enable efficient output of multiple primitive actions per model invocation. For data construction, we combine expert demonstrations with policy-dependent DAgger experience and develop a scalable synthesis pipeline that generates large-scale tasks for reinforcement learning. At the optimization level, a progressive IL-DAgger-RL pipeline advances from action imitation to task-level outcome optimization. Comprehensive experiments validate the effectiveness of these three aspects. We instantiate SimpleVLN across multiple MLLM backbones and model sizes, demonstrating its generality. SimpleVLN achieves 76.7% and 80.1% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE splits, respectively, substantially outperforming existing methods. These results show that the navigation capabilities of native MLLMs can be effectively unlocked without task-specific architectural designs.

items.title: Simulating the Clinical Encounter: Using AI Personas for Risk-Free Mental Health Assessment Practice
items.abstract: Mental health assessment requires students to navigate complex conversations involving depression, anxiety, mania, psychosis, suicide risk, and other sensitive clinical situations. Yet opportunities to repeatedly practice these conversations in a safe, low-stakes environment can be limited. This session demonstrates an innovative approach to using generative artificial intelligence as an interactive patient simulation tool in nursing education. Rather than using AI simply to generate written assignments or answer questions, students interact with AI-generated patient personas designed to exhibit specific psychiatric symptoms and communication patterns. Through spoken or conversational interactions, students practice conducting mental health assessments, asking therapeutic follow-up questions, recognizing clinical cues, and adapting their communication as an encounter unfolds. During this interactive session, participants will see a live demonstration of an AI-simulated mental health encounter and experience how thoughtfully constructed prompts can transform generative AI into a repeatable practice environment. Practical examples will illustrate how faculty can design patient personas representing conditions such as depression, mania, anxiety, and psychosis while incorporating appropriate educational guardrails. The session will also address the role of faculty oversight, limitations of AI-generated responses, and the importance of positioning AI simulation as preparation for, rather than a replacement for, authentic human clinical experiences. Participants will leave with a practical framework for creating AI patient personas and ideas for incorporating low-risk, repeatable conversational practice into their own nursing courses.

items.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations---a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent's desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q. At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent's reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.

items.title: Skill2Hire – An Intelligent AI-Powered Career Assistance Platform
items.abstract: Students preparing for technology-sector recruitment must manage resume preparation, job-description matching, vacancy discovery, interview practice, and industry updates. These activities are often spread over different platforms. This paper presents Skill2Hire, a modular AI-powered career assistance platform with five independent modules: an ATS-oriented Resume Builder, Resume Tailoring and Skill-Gap Analysis, Job Suggestions, a Mock Interview Simulator, and a Tech News Hub. The proposed system uses a React and TypeScript frontend, a Node.js and Express backend, MongoDB Atlas for persistent storage, and server-side large language model integration for selected language tasks. A rule-based ATS compatibility score estimates resume completeness, keyword alignment, skills coverage, structure, and formatting. Resume tailoring follows a “Zero Fake Skills” rule: missing qualifications are reported as skill gaps rather than inserted into the candidate’s resume. The interview module includes eligibility screening, aptitude assessment, technical interview, and behavioral HR stages. The paper describes the design, workflows, architecture, responsible-AI safeguards, and evaluation plan. Claims of quantitative performance are not treated as findings unless measurements can be reproduced. Keywords— Career assistance, Applicant Tracking System, resume tailoring, job recommendation, large language models, mock interview, skill-gap analysis.

items.title: Smartphone-based biological sex identification from palatal rugae images: a comparative transfer learning study of pretrained convolutional neural networks
items.abstract: Abstract Background Palatal rugae are distinct anatomical ridges on the anterior part of the palate that exhibit individual-specific morphological patterns, making them valuable markers for personal identification and forensic analysis. With advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning methods have emerged as effective tools for extracting discriminative features from medical and biometric images. This study investigates the potential of transfer learning-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for biological sex classification using palatal rugae images captured through a smartphone camera. Results All pretrained models successfully learned discriminative biological sex -related features from palatal rugae images. Among them, Residual network 50 (ResNet50) and Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG16) achieved the highest classification accuracy with optimal precision and recall, while EfficientNet-B0 and Dense Network 121 (DenseNet) demonstrated comparable but slightly lower performance. The Receiver Operating Curve (ROC curve) exhibited high Area under the Curve (AUC) values, confirming the strong separability between male and female classes. Conclusion The findings confirm that smartphone-based imaging combined with transfer learning offers a promising, low-cost, and non-invasive approach for biological sex identification using palatal rugae patterns, as an adjunct tool for forensic odontology. Among the evaluated models, ResNet50 showed the most robust performance. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and incorporating explainable Artificial Intelligence methods to support clinical and forensic applicability.

items.title: SmartTwin AI: An Explainable Predictive-Maintenance Decision-Support Framework for Smart Manufacturing
items.abstract: This research presents SmartTwin AI, a software-based framework for predictive maintenance in smart manufacturing. The study explores how machine-learning models can use industrial sensor measurements to identify potential machine failures and support maintenance decisions. Experiments were conducted using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset, which contains 10,000 records of machine operating conditions. Three machine-learning models were evaluated: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. The evaluation included precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrices. A threshold-tuning experiment was also performed to improve the detection of potential failures. The results show that the Random Forest model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.9653. After threshold tuning, the model achieved a recall of 79.41% on the test set, demonstrating a potential approach for identifying machines that may require maintenance. This work combines concepts from Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Engineering and Technology. It provides a reproducible software-based research workflow, experimental results, visualizations, and a proposed system architecture. Important limitation: The AI4I 2020 dataset is a synthetic benchmark dataset. The experiments were conducted on this dataset and do not represent a live deployment or a physical factory experiment. The proposed framework is a research prototype and requires further validation using real industrial data. The accompanying research paper and reproducibility materials document the methodology, results, limitations, and potential future work.

items.title: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents
items.abstract: Browser agents automate complex workflows by reading and acting on arbitrary page content, but this flexibility exposes them to prompt injection attacks and unintended data exfiltration. Recent work argues that LLM-driven browser agents erode traditional web security boundaries such as the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) by acting across origins with the user's authority and no built-in isolation. We argue that restoring SOP is neither sufficient (a same-origin public sink can leak private data) nor necessary (legitimate tasks require authorized cross-origin flows) for protecting the security of users. We propose SPIDES, which instead enforces information-flow control by gating primitive browser actions such as typing, clicking and navigating on labels propagated from element-level HTML confidentiality and integrity annotations. Untrusted and confidential content is masked from the agent's context, while policies block unauthorized flows, providing security guarantees against both prompt injection and data exfiltration that hold independently of the model driving the agent. To evaluate SPIDES and baseline defenses under a common threat model, we build MicroNet, a closed ecosystem of 28 interlinked websites with element-level ground-truth labels and paired benign/adversarial tasks. SPIDES achieves 0% attack success rate by design while retaining high task completion rate and autonomy. Our findings demonstrate that information-flow control is an effective technique to extend web security to browser agents, gaining on autonomy and utility against state-of-the-art baselines. The source code and data are openly accessible at https://github.com/microsoft/SPIDES.

items.title: Spiking Transformers and Event-Driven Foundation Models: Surrogate Gradient Dynamics, Spike-Driven Attention, and Neuromorphic Silicon Benchmarks
items.abstract: Standard digital Transformer architectures rely on dense matrix-matrix multiplications (GEMM) characterized by continuous-valued activations, generating massive thermal energy footprints and memory bandwidth bottlenecks during inference and training. In contrast, biological brains process complex spatio-temporal information via asynchronous, event-driven action potentials (spikes) with extraordinary thermodynamic efficiency. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) emulate this biological paradigm by communicating via discrete binary events, replacing energyintensive Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) operations with sparse Accumulate (AC) additions. However, extending spiking architectures to scale-invariant foundation models encounters three critical theoretical and architectural barriers: (1) Non-differentiable threshold-triggered spiking dynamics that prevent canonical backpropagation; (2) Temporal vanishing and exploding gradients across multi-timestep unfolded graphs; and (3) Quadratic complexity self-attention mechanisms that violate binary event sparsity. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal investigation and empirical benchmark of Spiking Transformers (Spikformers) and event-driven foundation models. We formalize surrogate gradient optimization under parameterized arctangent and fast-sigmoid relaxations, derive linear Spike-Driven Self-Attention (SDSA) operators utilizing pure binary sparse additions, and model asynchronous leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) dynamics across spatial-temporal horizons. Furthermore, we construct an empirical hardware-in-the-loop neuromorphic testbed benchmarking Spikformers against dense Vision Transformers (ViT) across Intel Loihi 2 neuromorphic processors, SynSense Speck vision sensors, and NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Our findings demonstrate that Spike-Driven Attention reduces computation energy consumption by 82.4% over standard ViT baselines while achieving 81.2% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with an average spike firing rate of 0.18 spikes per neuron per timestep. Finally, we formulate open challenges in all-spike autoregressive generation, neuromorphic on-chip continual plasticity, and multi-modal eventsensor fusion.

items.title: Strategic analysis of online pharmacy implementation: a scoping review and SWOT-based framework
items.abstract: The expansion of online pharmacies, a key development in digital health, has influenced both patient care and health system operations. Despite their benefits, these platforms face regulatory, infrastructural, and safety challenges. This study aimed to provide a strategic overview of online pharmacy implementation and propose operational strategies. A scoping review was conducted following the six-stage framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and June 2026. After screening 496 records, 37 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Data were analyzed using the framework analysis approach developed by Ritchie and Spencer and were subsequently categorized according to a SWOT framework and associated implementation strategies. Online pharmacies offer several potential advantages, including lower indirect costs, improved access to pharmaceutical services, and enhanced medication management. However, challenges such as digital inequalities, logistical constraints, and cybersecurity concerns remain significant. Key opportunities include integration with telemedicine, emerging regulatory frameworks, and the adoption of innovative technologies. Major threats involve regulatory gaps, counterfeit medicines, self-medication, and financial sustainability challenges. Eleven implementation strategies were identified to support the safe and sustainable development of online pharmacy services. Online pharmacies have the potential to serve as an important complement to health systems by reducing indirect patient costs, may contribute to improving equity in access, and enhancing the quality of services. Realizing this potential requires coherent policymaking, investment in infrastructure, and the use of novel technologies such as artificial intelligence.

items.title: Strategic Prevention of Occupational and Toxicological Risks in Moroccan Traditional Tanneries: From Risk Assessment to Operational Health and Safety Planning
items.abstract: The artisanal sector is a part of Morocco's second-largest employment and represents a major socioeconomic activity. However, it remains a major source of occupational exposure and environmental contamination, where preventive systems and regulatory enforcement are often insufficient. This study represents the fourth phase of a comprehensive research program on artisanal tanneries in Fez, based on the identification of hazards, the assessment of health effects, and the elaboration of initial preventive recommendations. Using reference data collected between 2017 and 2019, we assessed the current status of the implementation of workplace safety measures in 2025 through a contextual and operational analysis of workplace practices. Persistent improvements were observed in personal protective equipment use, hygiene conditions, and access to medical surveillance. Tannery workers frequently reported dermatological, respiratory, urinary, and musculoskeletal disorders, reflecting the need for regular medical monitoring of occupational exposure. An integrated strategic prevention plan is proposed, combining engineering controls, safer chemical management, worker training, and enhanced health surveillance. This framework provides a progressive model for improving occupational health and safety in artisanal tanneries, in line with the One Health approach.

items.title: Students Use of Generative AI Models for Health Information Seeking: Lessons from a Developing Country in Africa
items.abstract: This study investigated students’ use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) models for health information seeking in Nigeria. A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected through an online questionnaire administered to students in selected universities across the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria. A total of 308 valid responses were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The findings revealed that ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Claude were the most widely used generative AI models for health information seeking. Students frequently used AI tools for obtaining immediate health information, understanding diseases and symptoms, supporting academic research, and seeking mental health and wellness information. Convenience, ease of use, quick access to information, and free availability significantly influenced usage. Although respondents moderately trusted AI-generated health information, they emphasized the need to verify such information with healthcare professionals because of concerns about misinformation, contradictory responses, and privacy risks. The study further revealed that demographic variables had no significant influence on students’ use of generative AI models. The study concluded that generative AI models have become important health information tools among students despite associated credibility and technological challenges. The study recommended AI literacy programs, information verification training, ethical AI policies, and improved internet infrastructure in Nigerian universities.
